responsibilities.duty: Ensure no aide works without required TB documentation; review positive-test documentation; audit compliance.
Collect and file certificates, track due dates, send reminders, and notify the Scheduler of status.
Assign visits only to aides cleared for TB screening status.
Remove aides with possible TB symptoms from client contact and arrange coverage.
Complete exams on time, submit certificates, and report symptoms.

documentation: Practitioner's TB certificate after each exam (confidential health file)
Documentation of no risk of spreading disease for any positive result
Transferring-aide verification or prior certificate
TB tracking calendar
Exposure determination and bloodborne pathogen records where applicable
Quarterly audit record

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designee, and all employees, affiliated home care aides and volunteers whose records [AGENCY NAME] keeps
policies.purpose: To define what each personnel file contains, how files are kept secure and complete, and how [AGENCY NAME] can show CDSS that each aide meets the registry, clearance, TB and training requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a personnel file for every employee, affiliated aide and volunteer. Each aide file holds registry status, Live Scan clearance, TB certificate, training logs and the criminal-conviction statement, so that [AGENCY NAME] can give CDSS, on request, a complete list of affiliated aides and proof that each meets the requirements for registry clearance (HSC §1796.43), training (HSC §1796.44) and TB screening (HSC §1796.45), as required by HSC §1796.37(a)(5). The TB certificate stays on file after each exam (HSC §1796.45(d)). Training must be completed before the aide provides services, including 5 hours of entry-level training before presence with a client (HSC §1796.44). The Act sets no retention period for personnel records; as an operator standard, [AGENCY NAME] keeps each personnel file for at least 7 years after the person's separation. Files are kept secured and separate from client records.

definitions.definition: The set of records on each employee, aide or volunteer, kept in locked cabinets and/or access-controlled electronic storage.
A separately secured part of the file holding TB certificates and other medical information.
A current list of every affiliated aide showing registry, clearance, TB and training status, produced to CDSS on request.

procedures: The designee opens a personnel file for each person on the day an offer is accepted, using the Personnel File Checklist.

Each aide file must contain: application and resume; proof of age 18 or older; job description acknowledgment (JD-04); offer letter and conditions of employment (PER-01); employment eligibility and payroll documents required by law.
The file must also contain registry verification (printout or screenshot of cleared listing) and registration/renewal records (PER-03).
The file must contain Live Scan receipt, clearance confirmation, and the signed criminal-conviction statement (PER-04).
The file must contain the practitioner's TB certificate after each exam, and any documentation required for a positive result, kept in the confidential health section (PER-05).

The file must contain the training verification log showing entry-level training (2 hours orientation and 3 hours safety) completed before client contact, annual training of at least 5 hours each year, and, from January 1, 2027, dementia training (TRN-02 to TRN-05).
The file must contain the signed Abuse Reporting Acknowledgment (PER-02), confidentiality/HIPAA acknowledgment (CR-03), and receipt of the policies and employee handbook.
Performance evaluations, supervisory visit summaries, disciplinary notices and grievance records are filed in the file's general section (PER-09, SVC-03).
Separation documents, including the notice to CDSS where applicable, are added within 5 working days of separation (PER-10).
The designee does not allow any aide to be scheduled until the administrator initials the Personnel File Checklist showing all pre-contact items are complete.

Files are kept in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system at [ADDRESS]. Only the licensee, administrator and designee may access them; others only with the administrator's written approval. Access is logged.

Personnel files are stored separately from client records (REC-01). Client information is never placed in a personnel file except an incident summary needed for discipline, with identifiers minimized.

The designee maintains the Aide Compliance List and updates it at least weekly. The administrator audits at least 25% of aide files each quarter, and all files annually, and corrects gaps within 5 working days (GOV-05).

When CDSS requests the list of affiliated aides and proof of compliance, the administrator produces the Aide Compliance List and the supporting file documents promptly during inspection or request (GOV-07).
Employees may review their own file on request to the administrator, with the review documented, subject to law.

Files are retained at least 7 years after separation. After that period, the designee destroys them by shredding or secure electronic deletion, and records the destruction date. Files are not destroyed while a complaint, audit, claim or legal hold is pending.

responsibilities.duty: Approve file completeness before client contact, audit files, respond to CDSS requests, and enforce access limits.
Create and maintain files, maintain the Aide Compliance List, and manage retention and destruction.
Provide supervisory visit and evaluation documents for filing.
Provide accurate documents and update contact information and certifications.

documentation: Personnel File Checklist
Aide Compliance List
Access log
Quarterly audit records
Retention and destruction log

policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime, Travel Time, Mileage and Paid Sick Leave
policies.applies_to: All hourly employees, including affiliated home care aides; Scheduler / Registry and Billing Coordinator; administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure employees are paid correctly for all time worked, including travel time between clients, receive required overtime, are reimbursed for necessary expenses such as mileage, and earn paid sick leave.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is a third-party employer of home care workers. Under 29 CFR 552.109, it may not claim the federal companionship or live-in exemptions from minimum wage and overtime, and it does not do so. [AGENCY NAME] pays each employee at least the 2026 California state minimum wage of $16.90 per hour, or the higher local minimum wage that applies where the work is performed. It pays overtime as required by federal and California law; because California daily overtime rules and rules for live-in or 24-hour care are complex, [AGENCY NAME] has them reviewed by qualified employment counsel before offering any shift longer than 8 hours, live-in assignment or 24-hour care. Time traveling between clients during the workday is paid time, consistent with Department of Labor guidance. Under Labor Code §2802, [AGENCY NAME] reimburses necessary employee expenses, including mileage driven between clients and on client errands; the 2026 IRS rate of 72.5 cents per mile is the benchmark used. Employees accrue and may use paid sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year, as required by Labor Code §246. No employee is retaliated against for using sick leave, asking about pay or reporting a pay concern.

definitions.definition: An employer, such as an HCO, other than the individual or household receiving the services; it may not use the companionship or live-in exemptions.
All time an employee is under the employer's control or required to be on duty, including training, client visits, required meetings and travel between clients.
Time spent traveling from one client location to the next during the workday, which is paid.
Paid time off for the employee's or a family member's health needs, provided under Labor Code §246.
Repayment of the cost of using a personal vehicle for [AGENCY NAME] business, at the rate set under this policy.

procedures: The administrator sets each position's hourly rate in writing at hire so that it is never below the 2026 state minimum of $16.90 or the higher local minimum for the work location. Each January the administrator reviews the rates against state and local minimums, and corrects them by the effective date.
The offer letter states the hourly rate, pay period, pay day, overtime eligibility, mileage reimbursement and paid sick leave (PER-01).

The Scheduler records all hours worked through electronic visit verification and timekeeping (SVC-06): clock-in, clock-out, and travel between clients. Aides report missed clock-ins to the Scheduler the same day.
Paid time includes: visit time; travel time between clients; required training and orientation (TRN-02, TRN-03); required meetings; and time spent on client errands, including transport (PRG-04).
The Scheduler reviews timekeeping every pay period, resolves gaps, and obtains supervisor approval for edits. Employees may not be asked to work off the clock.

The Billing Coordinator calculates regular and overtime pay under federal and California rules, and does not apply any companionship or live-in exemption. Overtime is paid for all overtime hours worked, whether or not they were authorized in advance; unapproved overtime may lead to discipline but is still paid.
Before assigning any shift longer than 8 hours, live-in assignment or 24-hour care, the administrator confirms in writing that counsel has reviewed the pay method, and records the date of review.

Meal and rest periods are scheduled as required by California law; where an aide cannot take a required break because of client needs, the aide records it and the Billing Coordinator pays any premium owed.

Employees record miles driven between clients and on client errands in the mileage log or EVV app each day. Commuting between home and the first or last client of the day is handled under the written rule approved by counsel and kept in GOV-04.

The Billing Coordinator reimburses documented mileage at not less than the IRS standard rate in effect, 72.5 cents per mile for 2026, in the same pay period or the next, and shows it separately from wages.

Other necessary expenditures, such as supplies bought for a client at [AGENCY NAME]'s direction, are reimbursed within one pay period on receipt submission. Aides do not use personal funds for client purchases unless approved (CR-04).

Each employee earns paid sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year, as required by Labor Code §246. The Billing Coordinator tracks the balance and shows it on each pay statement or by other written notice.

An employee asks to use sick leave by notifying the Scheduler as early as possible; the Scheduler arranges coverage so no client visit is missed (SVC-05). [AGENCY NAME] does not require a replacement worker to be found as a condition of using leave.
The Billing Coordinator provides an itemized wage statement every pay period that shows hours, rates, overtime, deductions and reimbursements.

Employees report a pay or reimbursement concern to the Billing Coordinator or administrator. A written response is made within 10 working days, and corrections are paid promptly. Unresolved concerns follow PER-09.
The administrator audits payroll quarterly (sample of pay periods compared with EVV records) and corrects errors with back pay (GOV-05, GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Approve wage rates and ensure funds are available for payroll, overtime and reimbursements.
Set compliant rates, obtain counsel review for complex shifts, audit payroll, and prevent retaliation.
Record time, calculate pay and overtime, reimburse mileage, track sick leave and issue wage statements.
Approve time edits and ensure scheduling does not push employees into unpaid work.
Record time and mileage accurately, take scheduled breaks, and report errors.

documentation: Pay rate schedule and annual minimum wage review
EVV and timekeeping records
Mileage logs and reimbursement records
Paid sick leave balance records
Counsel review record for long shifts or live-in care
Itemized wage statements
Quarterly payroll audit

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All affiliated home care aides, Client Care Supervisor(s), Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, Administrator and designee(s), volunteers, and anyone else who has contact with clients or client information
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of conduct and professional boundaries so that clients are protected from exploitation, confusion about the aide's role, and breaches of privacy, and so that staff know what is expected of them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] requires every person who works for the agency to keep a professional relationship with clients and their families. This policy is part of the personnel policies required by CDSS form HCS 281, Section B3. The Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act does not itself prescribe a code of conduct, so the standards below are operator standards adopted by [AGENCY NAME]. Staff may not borrow money from, accept gifts from, or take over the finances of any client (see CR-04). Staff may not assist with medication beyond the self-administration support allowed in SVC-04. Staff may not make private side arrangements with clients or their families outside the agency. Staff must protect client confidentiality in person, by phone, and on social media (see CR-03). Violations are handled under PER-09, and any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under PER-02 and PRG-05. Each employee signs an acknowledgment of this policy at hire.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates the aide's paid caregiving role from a personal, financial, romantic or business relationship with a client or family member.

Any agreement, paid or unpaid, between an aide and a client or the client's family for services, money, goods or housing that is not made through [AGENCY NAME] and documented in the service agreement.

Limited help such as reminders or help opening containers, as described in SVC-04, with the client remaining in control of taking his or her own medication. It does not include selecting, preparing, measuring or giving medication.
Any information about a client, a client's family, the client's home, or other staff, including names, addresses, health conditions, schedules, photos and records.

procedures: At hire, the Administrator or designee reviews this policy with each new employee during orientation (see TRN-02). The employee signs the Conduct and Boundaries Acknowledgment, and a copy is placed in the personnel file (see PER-06).
Staff must treat clients with dignity and respect and use the client's preferred name. Staff may not use abusive, profane, discriminatory or demeaning language or behavior (see CR-05 and SAF-01).
Staff must not borrow money, property, vehicles, or anything of value from a client or family member, and must not lend their own money or property to a client.

Staff must not accept gifts, tips, bequests, or being named in a client's will, trust, or account, except as CR-04 expressly permits. Staff must tell the Client Care Supervisor the same day if a gift is offered, so the offer can be declined and documented.

Staff must not take over, manage or access a client's finances, bank or credit cards, PINs, checks, or online accounts. Shopping or errands are done only as set out in the service plan, with a receipt and the client's change returned and logged under CR-04.

Staff must not give, set up, measure, prepare, or select medication, and must not make decisions about medication. They may provide only the self-administration support described in SVC-04 and must document it.

Staff must not accept, request or arrange private work, pay, or services from a client or family outside [AGENCY NAME]. An aide who receives such an offer must report it to the Client Care Supervisor within one business day. This policy does not limit an aide's lawful right to seek other employment.

Staff must not engage in romantic or sexual contact or in a business, investment, or dating relationship with a client. They must not share personal problems with clients or ask a client for emotional or financial favors.
Staff must not use a client's phone, computer, vehicle, food, or supplies for personal purposes. They must not bring family, friends, pets or visitors into a client's home.

Staff must not work under the influence of alcohol, cannabis, or non-prescribed drugs, and must not smoke or vape in a client's home unless the client's own household rules allow it and the service plan does not prohibit it.
Staff may share client information only with people who need it to provide or supervise care, as set out in CR-03. Staff must not discuss clients in public places or with other clients.

Staff may not post photos, videos, names, locations or stories about clients, client homes, or care situations on social media, messaging groups or the internet, even if the client is not named. Staff may not ‘friend’ or message clients or family on personal social media accounts.
Staff may not photograph or record a client except as the client has authorized in writing and as the Administrator has approved for care purposes.

Staff must wear identification, dress appropriately, arrive on time, and follow the service plan and the scope limits in PRG-03. They must not perform tasks outside the plan, including medical tasks, that they are not assigned to do.

Staff must report any boundary concern to the Client Care Supervisor within one business day. They must report any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately under PER-02 and PRG-05. No employee may be retaliated against for reporting a concern in good faith.
The Client Care Supervisor documents each report, reviews it with the Administrator or designee, and decides whether to reassign the aide or begin discipline under PER-09.
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually under GOV-04 and updates the acknowledgment form as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Adopt and enforce this policy, review reports of violations, and apply discipline under PER-09.
Reinforce boundaries during supervisory visits, receive and document staff reports and gift offers, and report concerns to the Administrator.
Assign work only through the agency, decline requests for private arrangements, and report such requests.

responsibilities.role: Affiliated Home Care Aide and all staff
responsibilities.duty: Follow the standards above, avoid prohibited conduct, and report concerns and offers immediately.

documentation: Signed Conduct and Boundaries Acknowledgment in the personnel file
Written record of any gift offer, side-arrangement offer, or boundary concern and the action taken
Supervisory visit notes that address boundaries (see SVC-03)
Discipline records, if any (see PER-09)

policies.title: Discipline and Employee Grievance Procedure
policies.applies_to: All employees of [AGENCY NAME], including affiliated home care aides and office staff
policies.purpose: To provide a fair, consistent and documented process for correcting performance and conduct problems, and a channel for employees to raise complaints without fear of retaliation, while protecting clients and the agency's license.
policies.policy: CDSS form HCS 281, Section B3 requires personnel policies on hiring, discipline, grievance and mandated reporting. This policy supplies the discipline and grievance parts. [AGENCY NAME] uses progressive discipline, with a written record at each step. Serious misconduct may lead to immediate suspension or termination without earlier steps. Any allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation of a client results in the employee's immediate removal from client contact while it is investigated. Employees may bring a complaint to the Administrator or designee, and no one will be retaliated against for doing so in good faith. The agency also recognizes that CDSS may deny, suspend or revoke a license on the grounds listed in HSC §1796.38. Discipline decisions are therefore made with attention to client safety and licensing compliance. Nothing in this policy changes the terms of employment stated in the employee's offer letter or in PER-01, or creates a contract.

definitions.definition: A series of increasingly serious corrective steps: verbal counseling, written warning, final written warning or suspension, and termination.

Conduct that endangers a client, employee or the agency, including abuse, neglect, exploitation, theft or dishonesty, working under the influence, violence or threats, falsifying records or time, breach of confidentiality, and serious boundary violations.
A complaint by an employee about discipline, working conditions, treatment by a supervisor or co-worker, or application of agency policy.
Any adverse action, such as discipline, reduced hours, or harassment, taken because an employee raised a complaint or reported a concern in good faith.

procedures: The Client Care Supervisor or Administrator identifies a performance or conduct concern through supervisory visits, client or family feedback, timekeeping or EVV data, or staff reports, and documents the facts, date, and witnesses.

The supervisor meets privately with the employee, explains the concern, and listens to the employee's account before deciding on a response. The supervisor consults the Administrator or designee on any step beyond verbal counseling.
Step 1 is verbal counseling. The supervisor states the expectation, the support or training offered, and a time frame to improve. A dated note of the discussion goes into the personnel file.

Step 2 is a written warning. It describes the problem, prior counseling, the required corrective action, the deadline, and the consequence of not improving. The employee signs to acknowledge receipt. A signature shows receipt only, and a refusal to sign is noted.

Step 3 is a final written warning, with or without unpaid or paid suspension as permitted by law and PER-07. It is issued by the Administrator or designee and includes a corrective plan and a review date.
Step 4 is termination. The Administrator or designee decides after reviewing the file. The employee is separated under PER-10, including notice to CDSS.
Steps may be skipped, and an employee may be suspended or terminated immediately, for serious misconduct. The Administrator or designee approves in writing and documents the reason.

If a client, family member, or staff member alleges abuse, neglect or exploitation by an employee, the supervisor removes the employee from all client contact immediately. The Scheduler arranges coverage for clients (see SVC-05). The employee is placed on administrative leave, and pay is handled under PER-07 and applicable law.
The Administrator or designee ensures that mandated reports are made under PER-02 and PRG-05, and that the incident is recorded under SAF-02. The agency cooperates with investigators.

The Administrator or designee investigates promptly and documents interviews, evidence and conclusions. The employee returns to client contact only after the Administrator or designee documents the outcome and determines it is safe. Where a report is substantiated, the case is handled under Step 4 or as serious misconduct.

An employee who wants to raise a grievance may do so verbally or in writing to the Administrator or designee. If the grievance involves the Administrator, the employee may go to the licensee or governing body (see GOV-01) at [ADDRESS] or [PHONE].

The Administrator or designee acknowledges the grievance within two business days. The agency investigates and gives the employee a written response within ten business days, or states when a response will be given if more time is needed.
An employee who disagrees with the response may request review by the licensee or governing body in writing within five business days. The licensee gives a final written decision.

No employee may be retaliated against, threatened or treated differently for filing a grievance, reporting a concern, or cooperating with an investigation or with CDSS. Retaliation is serious misconduct.

Employees may also contact CDSS Home Care Services Branch directly at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov with concerns about licensing compliance. The Administrator posts this information with the license (see PRG-02).

The Administrator or designee reviews discipline and grievance trends at least quarterly as part of GOV-05, and addresses any pattern that could affect client safety or put the license at risk under HSC §1796.38.

responsibilities.duty: Approve serious discipline and terminations, investigate grievances and abuse allegations, decide when an employee may return to client contact, and ensure no retaliation.
Document performance concerns, issue verbal and written warnings with the Administrator's input, and remove an employee from client contact when an allegation arises.
Reassign clients and shifts promptly when an employee is removed from client contact.
Follow agency policies, cooperate with investigations, report concerns under PER-02, and use the grievance channel.

documentation: Counseling notes, written warnings, final warnings and termination letters in the personnel file (see PER-06)
Investigation file for any abuse, neglect or exploitation allegation, including the removal date and return-to-work decision
Grievance log and written responses, with dates
Incident reports and mandated reports (see SAF-02 and PRG-05)

policies.title: Aide Separation and Notice to CDSS
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designee, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, and every affiliated home care aide who leaves the agency
policies.purpose: To ensure that, when an affiliated home care aide stops working for the agency for any reason, CDSS is notified immediately, clients are protected, agency property and records are recovered, and the separation is fully documented.
policies.policy: When [AGENCY NAME] no longer employs an individual as an affiliated home care aide, it will immediately notify CDSS, as required by HSC §1796.43(a)(3), and will update the individual's status through the Guardian account. The same notice is required whether the aide resigns, is terminated, is laid off, or stops being assigned. The agency recovers client keys, access codes, records, and agency property, and reassigns affected clients without a gap in care. If the aide moves to another home care organization, the agency may support the aide's use of the tuberculosis certificate under HSC §1796.45(f), as described below. An exit checklist is completed and kept in the personnel file.

definitions.definition: The end of an individual's employment as an affiliated home care aide of [AGENCY NAME], whether voluntary or involuntary.
On the same business day the agency learns the separation is effective, or on the effective date, whichever is earlier.
The online account through the CDSS Care Provider Management Branch (Guardian) used to manage Home Care Aide registry information, including affiliation.
The licensed practitioner's certificate of tuberculosis examination that the agency keeps on file for each aide under HSC §1796.45(d).

procedures: The Administrator or designee records the separation date and reason in the personnel file as soon as an aide resigns, is terminated, or otherwise stops working. A resignation is requested in writing, but an aide who leaves without notice is still treated as separated once the Administrator or designee determines the aide will not return.

On the same business day the separation is effective, the Administrator or designee notifies CDSS that the agency no longer employs the individual as an affiliated home care aide, as required by HSC §1796.43(a)(3). The Administrator or designee uses the Guardian account and, if needed, contacts HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov.

The Administrator or designee updates the aide's affiliation in the Guardian account so that the registry shows the aide is no longer affiliated with [AGENCY NAME]. The date and time of notice, the method, and any confirmation number or screenshot are saved in the personnel file.
The Scheduler removes the aide from the schedule and EVV system immediately and cancels the aide's access to client information, scheduling apps and timekeeping (see SVC-06).

The Scheduler and Client Care Supervisor identify every client the aide served, the same day. They assign a qualified replacement aide, brief the replacement on the service plan, and notify each client or representative of the change (see SVC-05).
The Client Care Supervisor reviews open concerns, incidents, or unreported client information the aide has, and gets the aide's final documentation (see REC-01).

The Administrator or designee collects client keys, lockbox or door codes, ID badge, uniforms, equipment, and any agency or client property or records, and records each item on the exit checklist. Any keys or codes that cannot be recovered are changed or reported to the client, and the client is told.
The aide is reminded in writing that confidentiality obligations continue after separation (see CR-03 and PER-08).

Where the separation involves an allegation of abuse, neglect, or exploitation, the Administrator or designee also follows PER-02, PRG-05 and SAF-02, and reports to the proper authorities. The separation notice to CDSS under this policy is still made immediately and is not delayed for the investigation.
The final paycheck, accrued paid sick leave information and any other final-pay items are handled under PER-07 and applicable law, by the Administrator or the person responsible for payroll.

If the aide asks in writing to transfer the TB certificate to a new employer, the Administrator or designee provides the aide with a copy of the certificate, or verifies in writing to the new home care organization that [AGENCY NAME] holds the certificate and provides a copy, in line with HSC §1796.45(f). The request and the date of release are recorded. The agency does not release other health information.

The Administrator or designee completes the exit checklist, which covers CDSS notice, Guardian update, system access removal, client reassignment, property return, final pay, and TB certificate request. The Administrator signs and dates it.
The personnel file is closed and retained under PER-06 for the period stated there. The training log and TB certificate remain in the file (see TRN-05 and PER-05).

If a former aide is rehired, the agency repeats the hiring steps required by PER-01 to PER-05, including Live Scan, registry status and training verification. TB documentation is checked against HSC §1796.45.
The Administrator reviews separations quarterly as part of GOV-05 to identify patterns such as turnover or late notices to CDSS, and corrects any missed notice immediately.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure CDSS is notified immediately of each aide separation, sign the exit checklist, and decide on any abuse-related follow-up.
Act for the Administrator on CDSS notification and Guardian updates when the Administrator is unavailable.
Identify affected clients, ensure continuity of care, and brief replacement aides.
Remove the aide from schedules and systems, reassign shifts, and coordinate final timekeeping.
Return keys, badge, property and records, and complete any exit items.

documentation: Completed and signed exit checklist in the personnel file
Proof of CDSS notice and Guardian update, with date, time and method
Resignation letter or termination letter, as applicable
Record of client reassignment and client notifications
Record of property returned and any TB certificate release request

policies.title: Training Plan for Affiliated Home Care Aides
policies.applies_to: Administrator, designee, Client Care Supervisor, trainers, and all affiliated home care aides
policies.purpose: To state the agency's overall training plan for affiliated home care aides, including who conducts training, the written objectives, and the title and duration of each course, and to ensure that all required training is completed before an aide provides services.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 (8/15), p.15, Section B4(a), Training Plan for Affiliated Home Care Aides, submitted to CDSS at the time of application. For both entry-level and annual training, the plan states who will conduct the training, a written description of the objectives, and the title and duration of each course, as specified in HSC §1796.44. Under HSC §1796.44, the licensee must ensure that each aide completes training before providing services. [AGENCY NAME] will not assign an aide to any client until the five hours of entry-level training are complete and recorded. Each aide must then complete five hours of annual training. Training may be delivered online (HSC §1796.44(d)). The detailed content is in TRN-02 (entry-level) and TRN-03 (annual). The tracking log is in TRN-05, and a sample log is submitted with this plan. Dementia care training required from January 1, 2027, is described in TRN-04.

definitions.definition: The minimum five hours that an aide completes before presence with a client: two hours of orientation on the aide's role and terms of employment, and three hours of basic health and safety training.
A minimum of five hours each year that relates to core competencies and is population specific.
A person named in this plan, or an approved online provider, who delivers a course and attests to the aide's completion.
The record of each aide's courses, dates, hours, trainer and completion, described in TRN-05.

procedures: The Administrator designates the training lead. The agency lists each trainer by name and qualification in the Training Plan Summary below. The trainers for entry-level and annual courses are [TRAINER NAME AND QUALIFICATIONS] and, for online courses, [ONLINE TRAINING PROVIDER NAME].

Training Plan Summary, entry-level (total 5 hours): (a) Orientation: Role of the Caregiver and Terms of Employment, 2 hours, taught by [TRAINER NAME]; (b) Basic Health and Safety, including Infection Control and Emergency Procedures, 3 hours, taught by [TRAINER NAME]. The full objectives are in TRN-02.

Training Plan Summary, annual (total 5 hours): (a) Clients' Rights and Safety, 1 hour; (b) Responding to Daily Living Needs, 1 hour; (c) Reporting, Preventing and Detecting Abuse and Neglect, 1 hour; (d) Assisting with Personal Hygiene and Other Home Care Services, 1 hour; (e) Safe Transport of Clients (if the aide provides transportation) and population-specific topics for the clients the agency serves, 1 hour. The full objectives are in TRN-03. From January 1, 2027, the dementia content in TRN-04 is added.

Each course has a written objective statement, a title, a duration, a trainer, and a method (in person or online), kept in the training plan file. The Administrator submits the plan to CDSS with the application, with a sample verification log (see TRN-05).

The Scheduler checks the training log before adding any new aide to a client assignment and does not assign the aide until the Administrator or Client Care Supervisor confirms in the log that all five entry-level hours are complete.

For in-person training, the trainer takes a sign-in sheet that records the date, start and end time, topic and signatures. For online training, the provider's completion certificate showing the aide's name, course title, date and hours is saved. Only time spent in the course counts toward hours.

The aide must pass a short quiz or demonstration at the end of each course, using a written test or supervisor observation, so that learning objectives can be shown to be met. A trainer reviews missed items with the aide.

The Client Care Supervisor tracks each aide's annual training due date, set as 12 months from the date of hire, and reminds the aide at 60 days and again at 30 days before the due date. Entry-level hours are not counted toward the annual five hours.
An aide who has not completed the annual training by the due date is not scheduled until the missing hours are completed, unless the Administrator documents otherwise in line with HSC §1796.44.
The Administrator reviews each trainer's qualifications and the course content annually, updating content for law changes, population served and quality findings (see GOV-05).
Training records are filed under TRN-05 and in the personnel file (see PER-06), where they are available to CDSS inspectors at any time.
The Administrator reviews this plan at least annually under GOV-04 and revises it as the law or the agency's population changes.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure each aide completes training before providing services, approve trainers and course content, and keep the plan current.
Deliver or arrange trainings, observe competency, and track annual due dates.
Confirm training completion in the log before assigning a new aide.
Attend and complete all assigned training and keep completion certificates.

documentation: Written training plan, with trainer names, objectives, course titles, and hours, kept in the agency file and filed with the HCS 281 application
Sample and actual training verification logs (see TRN-05)
Sign-in sheets, online completion certificates, and quiz or competency records
Trainer qualification records

policies.title: Entry-Level Training (5 Hours Before Client Contact)
policies.applies_to: All newly hired affiliated home care aides, the Client Care Supervisor, the Scheduler, and trainers
policies.purpose: To ensure every new affiliated home care aide completes the required five hours of entry-level training before being present with any client.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 (8/15), p.15, Section B4 – Entry-Level Training, item B4(b). An affiliated home care aide must complete a minimum of five hours of entry-level training before presence with a client (HSC §1796.44(b)). The training includes two hours of orientation on the aide's role as a caregiver and the terms of employment, and three hours of basic health and safety training, including infection control and emergency procedures. The licensee must ensure the training is completed before the aide provides services (HSC §1796.44(a)). Training may be online (HSC §1796.44(d)). The agency does not allow an aide to shadow, observe, or be present with a client until all five hours are complete and recorded in the training log. As an additional operator standard, not a state requirement, the agency requires a supervised competency check on core tasks before the first solo assignment.

definitions.definition: Being in a client's home or with a client in any role, including shadowing or observing, before the entry-level training is complete.
Two hours covering the aide's role as a caregiver and the terms of employment.
Three hours covering basic safety precautions, infection control and emergency procedures.
A supervised demonstration of core tasks by the aide before the first solo assignment, which is an agency standard.

procedures: After the offer is accepted and clearance steps in PER-03 and PER-04 are done, the Client Care Supervisor schedules the aide's entry-level training date, in person or online. The aide is told in writing that no client contact is allowed until training is done.

Orientation (2 hours). The trainer covers: the aide's role and limits as a non-medical caregiver (PRG-03); terms of employment, pay, hours and sick leave (PER-07); conduct and boundaries (PER-08); discipline and grievance (PER-09); mandated reporting duties (PER-02); client rights (CR-01); confidentiality (CR-03); and how to use the schedule and EVV (SVC-06). Objectives: the aide can describe the role, what tasks are in and out of scope, and the employment terms.

Basic Health and Safety (3 hours). The trainer covers: basic safety precautions, including fall prevention, safe lifting and body mechanics, home hazards and fire safety; infection control, including hand hygiene, standard precautions, glove use, cleaning and disinfecting, and handling soiled items (SAF-03); and emergency procedures, including when to call 911, how to respond to a fall, choking or medical emergency, reporting to the Client Care Supervisor (SVC-07), and disaster plans (SAF-04). Objectives: the aide can demonstrate hand hygiene and name the steps in an emergency.
The trainer or online provider records attendance with a sign-in sheet or completion certificate showing the aide's name, course title, date, hours, and trainer.
The aide completes a short written quiz or demonstration for each course. The trainer reviews any missed items and records the result.
The trainer or Client Care Supervisor enters each course, the date, the hours and the trainer in the training verification log (TRN-05) the same day, and the aide initials the entry.

Competency check (operator standard). Before the first solo assignment, the Client Care Supervisor observes the aide perform core tasks, such as hand hygiene, safe transfer assistance or standby help, assisting with personal hygiene, and emergency response steps, using a checklist. The aide repeats any task that is not performed correctly.

The Administrator or Client Care Supervisor confirms in the log that all five entry-level hours and the competency check are complete, signs and dates the confirmation, and releases the aide to the Scheduler.
The Scheduler does not assign the aide to any client, visit or orientation shift until the release in step 8 is on file.
If the aide misses any part of the training, the aide completes the missing part before being scheduled. Partial hours are not rounded up.
Records are filed in the personnel file (PER-06) and in TRN-05, and are available to CDSS inspectors during inspections (GOV-07).
The Administrator reviews the content annually and updates it for changes in law or in the agency's services (TRN-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensure no aide is present with a client before the five hours are complete, and approve the release.
Deliver or arrange training, grade quizzes, perform the competency check, and complete the log.
Verify the release in the log before any assignment.
Attend the full training, participate in the competency check, and sign the log.

documentation: Training verification log entries for orientation and basic health and safety (TRN-05)
Sign-in sheets or online completion certificates
Quiz results and competency checklist
Signed release to schedule, filed in the personnel file

policies.title: Annual Training (5 Hours Per Year)
policies.applies_to: All affiliated home care aides, the Client Care Supervisor, the Scheduler, and trainers
policies.purpose: To ensure every affiliated home care aide completes at least five hours of core-competency, population-specific training each year, covering the topics required by law.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 (8/15), p.15, Section B4 – Annual Training, item B4(c). Each affiliated home care aide must complete a minimum of five hours of annual training that relates to core competencies and is population specific (HSC §1796.44(c)). The proposed training includes, but is not limited to, these topics: clients' rights and safety; how to provide for and respond to a client's daily living needs; how to report, prevent, and detect abuse and neglect; how to assist a client with personal hygiene and other home care services; and how to safely transport a client, if applicable. Training may be online (HSC §1796.44(d)). Beginning January 1, 2027, a dementia care topic is added to annual training under SB 412 (see TRN-04). Annual training is separate from the five hours of entry-level training in TRN-02.

definitions.definition: A basic skill or area of knowledge every home care aide needs to give safe, respectful non-medical care.
Training tailored to the clients the agency serves, such as older adults, persons with disabilities, persons with dementia, or those with mobility limits.
The 12-month period starting on the aide's date of hire and each anniversary after that, used by [AGENCY NAME] to track the five hours.

procedures: Each December, the Administrator and Client Care Supervisor review the agency's client population, incident reports, supervisory findings, and law changes, and set the annual training calendar and course list. Population-specific topics are chosen based on this review.
The training year for each aide runs from the hire date. The Client Care Supervisor enters each aide's due date in the training verification log (TRN-05).

Clients' Rights and Safety (1 hour). Objectives: the aide can list client rights (CR-01), explain privacy and dignity, describe how to respect choices, and describe home safety practices and when to report a concern.

Daily Living Needs (1 hour). Objectives: the aide can describe how to provide for and respond to a client's daily living needs, such as meals, mobility, housekeeping and routines, in line with the service plan (SVC-02) and within the limits of PRG-03.

Reporting, Preventing and Detecting Abuse and Neglect (1 hour). Objectives: the aide can recognize signs of physical, emotional and financial abuse, neglect, self-neglect and exploitation, explain the aide's own reporting duties (PER-02, PRG-05), and describe how to prevent abuse (SAF-01).

Assisting with Personal Hygiene and Other Home Care Services (1 hour). Objectives: the aide can describe safe, dignified bathing, grooming, toileting and dressing help, can apply infection control (SAF-03), and can document the care provided.

Safe Transport of Clients and population-specific topics (1 hour). If the aide provides transportation, the aide is trained on safe transport under PRG-04, including loading, seat belts, and emergencies. If the aide does not provide transportation, this hour is used on a population-specific topic, such as fall prevention or communicating with clients with cognitive or sensory impairment.
Training is delivered by [TRAINER NAME AND QUALIFICATIONS] in person or by [ONLINE TRAINING PROVIDER NAME]. Online courses must show the aide's name, title, date and hours.

The trainer records attendance, and the aide completes a short quiz. The trainer or Client Care Supervisor enters the courses, dates, hours and trainer in the training verification log (TRN-05) the same day.

The Client Care Supervisor reminds each aide at 60 and 30 days before the due date. An aide who has not completed all five hours by the due date is not scheduled until the remaining hours are completed.
Starting January 1, 2027, the Administrator adds the dementia care content described in TRN-04 to the annual curriculum and updates the training plan (TRN-01) before that date.
Records are filed in the personnel file (PER-06) and kept for inspection (GOV-07).
The Administrator reviews the annual training outcomes as part of quality assurance (GOV-05) and updates the plan for the next year.

responsibilities.duty: Approve the annual training calendar, ensure each aide completes five hours each year, and update content for law changes.
Deliver or arrange the courses, track due dates, record completion, and send reminders.
Check training status in the log before scheduling, and hold assignments for aides who are overdue.
Complete the full five hours by the due date and keep certificates.

documentation: Training verification log showing annual courses, dates, hours, and trainers (TRN-05)
Sign-in sheets, online completion certificates and quiz results
Annual training calendar and course objectives
Reminder notices and records of any aide held from scheduling

policies.title: Dementia Care Training (Effective January 1, 2027)
policies.applies_to: All affiliated home care aides employed by [AGENCY NAME], the Client Care Supervisor, the Administrator, and whoever maintains the training log.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] meets the annual training requirement for the special care needs of clients with dementia that takes effect January 1, 2027, and that aides who serve clients with dementia are trained first.
policies.policy: Beginning January 1, 2027, the annual training of every affiliated home care aide employed by [AGENCY NAME] will include the special care needs of clients with dementia (HSC §1796.44(c)(6), added by SB 412). The 5-hour entry-level training and the 5-hour annual training minimums in HSC §1796.44 are unchanged. Dementia content is therefore a required topic inside the annual training, not an extra requirement on top of the 5-hour minimum. [AGENCY NAME] may require more hours. The bill digest describes dementia training both before providing care and annually, while the chaptered text lists it in the annual training. Until counsel confirms in writing whether a pre-service component is required, [AGENCY NAME] will apply this operator standard: an aide is assigned first to clients with dementia only after completing the dementia module. The training plan (TRN-01) and the training verification log (TRN-05) will be updated before January 1, 2027. This policy does not itself satisfy a specific HCS 281 checklist item. It supports the training plan under HCS 281 item B4.

definitions.definition: The agency-approved training unit on the special care needs of clients with dementia, delivered in person or online.
The minimum 5 hours of core-competency and population-specific training each aide completes every year under HSC §1796.44(c).
The 5 hours (2 hours orientation, 3 hours safety) completed before an aide is present with a client (HSC §1796.44(b)).

procedures: The Administrator will ask [AGENCY NAME]'s legal counsel, by [DATE BEFORE 1/1/2027], to confirm in writing whether HSC §1796.44(c)(6) requires a pre-service dementia component in addition to the annual component. The answer will be filed in the policy file under GOV-04.

If counsel says a pre-service component is required, the Administrator will add it to the onboarding sequence in TRN-02 before January 1, 2027, without reducing the 2-hour orientation or 3-hour safety minimums.

The Client Care Supervisor will select or develop the dementia module content. It will cover the special care needs of clients with dementia, including communication, behavior changes, safety and wandering, daily living support, and reporting concerns.
The Client Care Supervisor will name the trainer or training organization for the module and record its qualifications in the training plan (TRN-01).
Before January 1, 2027, the Administrator will update the training plan (TRN-01) and the sample and working training verification log (TRN-05) to show the dementia topic.
From January 1, 2027, each aide's annual training plan for the year will include the dementia module. The 5-hour annual total will be verified before the aide's anniversary of hire or registration.

Operator standard: when assigning aides, the Scheduler will identify clients whose assessment (SVC-01) or service plan (SVC-02) notes dementia or a cognitive impairment. The Scheduler will schedule dementia-module completion first for the aides assigned to those clients.

The Scheduler will not assign an aide who has not completed the dementia module to a client with a known dementia diagnosis unless the Client Care Supervisor documents why no trained aide is available and arranges for the aide to complete the module within a time the Client Care Supervisor sets.
The Client Care Supervisor will confirm each completion on the training verification log (TRN-05) with date, hours, trainer or organization, and location or website.
The Client Care Supervisor will run a monthly report of aides with no recorded dementia module and give it to the Administrator.
The Administrator will review the dementia module content each year, using aide and client feedback and any change in the law, and record the review under GOV-04.

New aides hired on or after January 1, 2027 will complete entry-level training (TRN-02) first. They will complete the dementia module within their first annual training period and, under the operator standard above, before being assigned to a client with dementia.

responsibilities.duty: Obtains counsel's confirmation, updates the training plan and log before 1/1/2027, and ensures compliance.
Selects the module, trains or arranges training, and verifies completion.
Identifies clients with dementia and assigns trained aides first.
Completes the dementia module on time and applies it in client care.

documentation: Counsel's written confirmation on the pre-service question
Updated training plan (TRN-01) and training verification log (TRN-05)
Dementia module outline, trainer qualifications and attendance records
Monthly dementia-training completion report
Documented exceptions under the assignment standard

policies.title: Training Verification Log and Training Records
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, Client Care Supervisor, trainers, and all affiliated home care aides.
policies.purpose: To record and verify that every affiliated home care aide completes the entry-level and annual training required by HSC §1796.44 before providing services, and to provide the sample training verification log required with the application.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 item B4(d) — Sample Training Verification Log. [AGENCY NAME] keeps a training verification log for every affiliated home care aide, and a sample is included with the training plan. At a minimum, the log contains: (1) the employee's name; (2) hire date; (3) position title; (4) registration date; (5) training title and a brief description of the topics covered; (6) the month/day/year the training was completed; (7) the training hours received; (8) the instructor/trainer's first and last name (if in-person training); (9) the organization delivering the training; and (10) the location of the training or, if online, the website. The licensee must ensure each aide completes training before providing services (HSC §1796.44). An aide may not be present with a client until the 5 hours of entry-level training (2 hours orientation, 3 hours safety) are logged and verified. Each aide must also log at least 5 hours of annual training each year, and online training is allowed (HSC §1796.44(d)).

definitions.definition: The per-employee record listing each training completed, with the data fields required by HCS 281 item B4(d).
The date the aide was registered on the Home Care Aide Registry by CDSS.
The agency, vendor, school or website provider that delivered the training.

procedures: On the employee's hire date, the Client Care Supervisor opens a training verification log for the employee. The log is pre-filled with the employee's name, hire date and position title (for example, Affiliated Home Care Aide).
When CDSS registers the aide, the Client Care Supervisor enters the registration date on the log (see PER-03).

For each training event, the trainer or the Client Care Supervisor enters the training title and a brief description of the topics covered, such as "Orientation: role of the aide and terms of employment" or "Safety: basic safety precautions, emergency procedures, infection control."
The entry gives the month/day/year the training was completed and the number of hours received. Hours are recorded as actually completed. No credit is given for partial or unattended sessions.
For in-person training, the log shows the instructor's first and last name, and the instructor signs or initials the entry.
The log shows the organization delivering the training, whether [AGENCY NAME] or an outside provider.

The log shows the location of the training. For online training, the log shows the specific website or platform. The aide submits the completion certificate or screenshot, which is attached to the file.
The aide signs or initials each entry to acknowledge attendance. The Client Care Supervisor verifies the entry against the sign-in sheet or certificate within 2 business days of completion.

Before the aide's first client contact, the Client Care Supervisor confirms that entry-level training totals at least 5 hours (2 orientation, 3 safety) and signs a "cleared for client contact" entry. The Scheduler may not assign the aide until this entry exists.

The Client Care Supervisor tracks each aide's annual training. Each aide must complete at least 5 hours each year covering clients' rights and safety, daily living needs, reporting/preventing/detecting abuse and neglect, personal hygiene help, and safe transport if transportation is provided. From January 1, 2027 the topics also include dementia care (TRN-04).

The Client Care Supervisor reviews all logs monthly. Aides who are within 60 days of their annual deadline are notified in writing, and overdue aides are reported to the Administrator for schedule action.
Completed logs and supporting certificates are filed in the personnel record (PER-06) and kept in a form that can be produced promptly during a CDSS inspection (GOV-07).

The Administrator reviews the log template once a year and updates it when training requirements change. A blank sample log is attached to the training plan (TRN-01) and filed with the HCS 281 application.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains logs, verifies entries, clears aides for client contact, and tracks annual training.
Records topics, hours and the instructor's name, and signs the entry.
Attends training, signs the log, and submits online certificates.
Reviews compliance monthly and makes the logs available to CDSS.

documentation: Training verification log for each aide with all ten required fields
Sample training verification log attached to the training plan
Sign-in sheets and online completion certificates
"Cleared for client contact" entry
Monthly log review record

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.applies_to: The licensee, Administrator, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler and all staff who describe or deliver [AGENCY NAME]'s services.
policies.purpose: To state what [AGENCY NAME] does, where, when, for whom, and how affiliated home care aides are assigned and supervised, as required in the HCS 281 program description (item B5), and to keep that description accurate.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is a Home Care Organization licensed by CDSS Home Care Services Branch under the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act. It arranges non-medical home care services for clients through affiliated home care aides it employs who are listed on the registry (HSC §1796.12(a), (j), (n)). The program description contains: services (PRG-03 and PRG-04), service area (PRG-06), hours (PRG-02), client population, and the assignment and supervision of aides. Services are non-medical only. [AGENCY NAME] serves clients aged [AGE RANGE] who cannot perform the services themselves because of age or disability. Payer model: [PRIVATE-PAY ONLY / PRIVATE-PAY AND MEDI-CAL MANAGED CARE PLAN CLIENTS UNDER CONTRACT WITH PLANS]. Entities that are not Home Care Organizations under HSC §1796.17 — licensed home health agencies and hospices, IHSS individual providers, employment agencies that only refer independent aides, and DDS-vendored organizations — are not covered by this program. [AGENCY NAME] does not operate as any of them. This policy supports HCS 281 item B5 (Program Description).

definitions.definition: Non-medical services to a client who cannot perform them because of age or disability, such as bathing, dressing, meals, housekeeping, transportation and companionship (HSC §1796.12(n)).
A person 18 or older who is employed by an HCO and listed on the registry (HSC §1796.12(a)).
The HCO places and supervises its employed aides to deliver services to clients (HSC §1796.12(j)).

procedures: Before opening, the Administrator drafts the program description with these sections: services, service area, business hours, client population, aide assignment, and supervision. A copy is filed with the HCS 281 application.

The Administrator states in the description whether [AGENCY NAME] serves only private-pay clients or also clients paid through Medi-Cal managed care plans, and ensures actual practice matches (SVC-09).
The program description lists each basic and optional service offered and states whether transportation is offered (PRG-03, PRG-04).
The service area section lists counties and areas served (PRG-06). The Scheduler declines referrals outside this area unless the Administrator approves a change.

The Client Care Supervisor completes an intake and assessment (SVC-01) for every referral to confirm that the client's needs are non-medical and within the program description. Requests for skilled nursing or therapy are declined and referred to a licensed provider.

The Scheduler assigns aides based on the service plan, aide qualifications and training (including the dementia standard in TRN-04), availability, travel distance and client preferences, and documents the match in the schedule record (SVC-05).
Only employed aides who are registered, cleared and trained (PER-03, PER-04, TRN-05) are assigned to clients.
Each client is supervised under SVC-03. The Client Care Supervisor makes supervisory contacts and visits and reports to the Administrator.
The Administrator reviews the program description at least once a year and whenever services, area, hours, population or payer model change. Reviews are recorded under GOV-04.

When a change is material, such as a new service, a change of payer model, a new location or a change in hours, the Administrator updates the description and notifies CDSS Home Care Services Branch before implementing the change where possible. Fee and notice steps are in GOV-02.
The Administrator ensures that advertising, the website and client materials do not describe services outside the program description (GOV-02).
Staff give the current program description, or a summary of it, to any person who requests it.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the program description and any material change.
Maintains and updates the description and notifies CDSS of material changes.
Screens referrals against the program description and supervises aides.
Assigns aides and confirms the service area.

documentation: Current program description
Dated review and revision log (GOV-04)
Copies of notices to CDSS about material changes
Referral decline records for out-of-scope or out-of-area requests

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Business Hours and Posting of License
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, designee, office staff, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler, and the on-call staff member.
policies.purpose: To establish and post [AGENCY NAME]'s business hours and license, to make staff available during those hours, and to provide after-hours contact for clients and aides.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 item B5(a) — Program Description element: Business Hours. [AGENCY NAME]'s business hours are [DAYS AND HOURS] at [ADDRESS]. These hours are stated in the program description (PRG-01). [AGENCY NAME] posts its license, business hours and any other information CDSS requires at the place of business in a conspicuous location visible to both clients and affiliated aides (HSC §1796.42(a)). CDSS may enter the Home Care Organization during posted business hours, with or without advance notice (HSC §1796.53). A staff member with authority to speak for [AGENCY NAME] and to provide records is available during all posted hours. Outside business hours, clients and aides can reach an on-call contact at [AFTER-HOURS PHONE].

definitions.definition: The days and hours shown on the posted notice and in the program description during which the office is open and staffed.
The designated staff member who answers client and aide calls outside business hours.

procedures: The Administrator sets the business hours in the program description (PRG-01) and uses the same hours everywhere they appear: posting, service agreement, website, and client materials.

On the day the license is received, the Administrator posts the original license, the business hours and any other CDSS-required information at [ADDRESS] in a conspicuous location visible to clients and aides, such as the reception area. The posting is not placed in a private office.
The Administrator checks the posting weekly and replaces it immediately if it is damaged, outdated or missing.

A staff member authorized to receive CDSS inspectors, and able to produce personnel, training, client and other records, is on the premises throughout posted business hours. The Administrator or a designee named on the HCS 308 is reachable by phone if not present (GOV-07).
If CDSS arrives during posted hours, staff admit the inspectors without delay and follow GOV-07. Staff do not ask inspectors to return later.
The office telephone is answered by a person or a voicemail that gives the business hours, the after-hours number and the emergency instruction (call 911 for emergencies).
The Administrator assigns an on-call staff member for every night, weekend and holiday outside business hours. The on-call roster is posted internally and updated weekly.
The on-call staff member returns calls from clients and aides promptly, handles urgent schedule gaps (SVC-05), and records each after-hours call in the call log by the next business day.
Clients receive the business hours and after-hours number in the service agreement (CR-06) and on their care-plan binder. Aides receive them at orientation (TRN-02).
Emergencies in the home are handled under SVC-07. After-hours reports of abuse, neglect or injury are escalated to the Administrator immediately (SAF-02, PRG-05).

If the business hours change, the Administrator updates the posting, program description and all client and aide materials, and notifies CDSS under GOV-02 before the change takes effect where possible.

If the place of business moves, the Administrator submits the change-of-location notice to CDSS with the $100 change-of-location fee (GOV-02). The license and hours are posted at the new location when it opens.
The Administrator reviews this policy annually and keeps proof of posting, such as a dated photograph, in the compliance file.

responsibilities.duty: Sets hours, posts the license and notices, and makes CDSS notifications.
Acts for the Administrator in his or her absence during posted hours.
Answer calls, admit CDSS and log calls.
Covers after-hours contacts and escalates urgent matters.

documentation: Posted license and business-hours notice with dated photograph
On-call roster
After-hours call log
Notices to CDSS of changes in hours or location and fee receipts

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Basic and Optional Services; Scope — What Aides May and May Not Do
policies.applies_to: All affiliated home care aides, the Client Care Supervisor, the Scheduler, intake staff, and anyone who markets or describes [AGENCY NAME]'s services.
policies.purpose: To define the non-medical basic and optional services [AGENCY NAME] provides and to set clear limits on what aides may and may not do.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 item B5(b) — Program Description element: Description of the basic and optional services provided by the Home Care Organization, which includes but is not limited to transportation services. [AGENCY NAME] provides non-medical home care services only, for clients who cannot perform them because of age or disability (HSC §1796.12(n)). Basic services are: bathing, dressing, feeding, exercising, hygiene and grooming, transferring, ambulating, positioning, and toileting and incontinence care. Optional services are: housekeeping, meal preparation, laundry, shopping, correspondence, phone calls, companionship and transportation. Transportation is described in PRG-04. Each client receives only the services listed in his or her service plan (SVC-02). Aides may assist with self-administered medication only. Aides may not assist with any medication that would otherwise require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional. Skilled nursing and therapy require a different license, and [AGENCY NAME] will not provide or advertise them.

definitions.definition: Personal-care tasks of daily living listed above that [AGENCY NAME] offers to clients.
Household, errand, social and transportation services offered when listed in the client's service plan.
A medication the client takes or applies by himself or herself, with the aide giving only non-medical assistance such as a reminder.
Nursing, therapy or other services requiring a licensed health care professional.

procedures: The Administrator lists the basic and optional services in the program description, and the Client Care Supervisor uses that list as the only menu of services in the service agreement (CR-06) and service plan (SVC-02).
During intake and assessment (SVC-01), the Client Care Supervisor checks each requested task against this policy. Each task is marked as accepted, declined, or referred to a licensed provider.

Basic services are provided according to the service plan: bathing, dressing, feeding, exercising, hygiene and grooming, transferring, ambulating, positioning, and toileting and incontinence care. Aides perform them only after training and instruction on the client's specific needs.
Optional services are added only if the client agrees in writing and the service is listed in the service plan.

Medication: aides may assist with self-administered medication only. Examples of acceptable assistance are reminding the client of a scheduled time, bringing the client's own labeled container to the client, and helping the client who is able to take the medication himself or herself. The Client Care Supervisor documents the task in the service plan (SVC-04).

Aides must not administer medication or assist with medication that requires administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional. Examples are injections, deciding doses, adjusting doses, and any medication the client cannot self-direct. The aide declines and calls the Client Care Supervisor immediately.

Aides do not perform skilled nursing or therapy tasks. Examples are wound care, injections, tube feeding, and clinical assessment. If a client needs such care, the Client Care Supervisor tells the client or representative that a licensed provider is required and helps the client find one (SVC-07, SVC-08).

An aide who is asked by a client or family to do a task outside the service plan says that he or she will check with the office, does not perform the task, and reports the request to the Client Care Supervisor the same day.
The Client Care Supervisor responds to each out-of-plan request within one business day. The response is to add the task to the plan if allowed, or to decline it and document the reason.

If a client's needs change, the Client Care Supervisor performs a reassessment and updates the service plan (SVC-02). If needs have moved beyond non-medical care, the Client Care Supervisor starts the discharge or referral process under SVC-08.
Advertising, website content and client materials are reviewed by the Administrator before use so that they do not describe or imply skilled nursing, therapy or other medical services (GOV-02).
Aides are trained at orientation (TRN-02) and annually (TRN-03) on the scope of services, and each aide signs a scope-of-practice acknowledgment kept in the personnel file (PER-06).
Violations of this policy are discipline matters under PER-09. If a client was harmed, they are also incidents under SAF-02.

responsibilities.duty: Keeps the service list accurate and reviews advertising for scope.
Screens tasks, writes service plans, answers aide questions, and handles out-of-scope requests.
Performs only service-plan tasks and refuses and reports out-of-scope tasks.
Explains the service menu to callers and refers medical requests to the Client Care Supervisor.

documentation: Program description service list
Service agreement and service plan task list
Scope-of-practice acknowledgment signed by each aide
Record of declined or referred tasks
Advertising review record

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Transportation Services and Safe Transport of Clients
policies.applies_to: Affiliated home care aides who transport clients, the Client Care Supervisor, the Scheduler, and the Administrator.
policies.purpose: To state how [AGENCY NAME] provides transportation as a home care service and to protect clients and aides when an aide drives a client.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 item B5(b) — Program Description element: Description of the basic and optional services provided by the Home Care Organization, which includes but is not limited to transportation services. Transportation is a listed home care service (HSC §1796.12(n)). [AGENCY NAME] offers transportation as an optional service, as stated in the program description (PRG-01), for errands, shopping and appointments in the service area, when it is in the client's service plan. If transportation is offered, annual training for aides must cover safe transport (HSC §1796.44(c)). Operator standard: an aide may drive a client only if he or she holds a valid driver's license, has vehicle insurance, and passes a safe-vehicle check. Aides are reimbursed for mileage under Labor Code §2802 (see PER-07). All persons in the vehicle use seat belts, wheelchairs are properly secured, and no client is transported against the client's or family's wishes. Clients with disabilities are treated without discrimination in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.) (CR-05). This is non-emergency, non-medical transportation. [AGENCY NAME] is not an ambulance or medical transport provider.

definitions.definition: A documented review confirming the vehicle has working brakes, lights, tires, seat belts and horn, is registered and clean, and has no known unrepaired safety defect.
Driving a client to destinations such as shopping, appointments and social outings, without medical monitoring.

procedures: The Administrator states in the program description whether transportation is offered. Aides may transport a client only if it is written in the client's service plan (SVC-02) with the client's or representative's consent.

Before an aide is approved to transport, the Client Care Supervisor copies and verifies the aide's valid driver's license and proof of current vehicle insurance, and files them in the personnel record (PER-06). Expiration dates are tracked, and an aide whose license or insurance lapses is removed from transport duties immediately.

The Administrator confirms with the insurance carrier that [AGENCY NAME]'s coverage (GOV-03) and the aide's personal coverage address use of a vehicle for client transport, and files the confirmation.

Before first use, and again [FREQUENCY, e.g., every 12 months], the Client Care Supervisor or the aide completes a documented safe-vehicle check on the aide's own vehicle. Aides who drive a client's vehicle do so only with the client's permission, with the vehicle's insurance verified, and after a basic safety check.
Aides complete safe-transport training in annual training (TRN-03) and training is logged under TRN-05.
Before each trip, the aide confirms the destination, the pickup and return times, and any mobility needs. The aide makes sure the client has needed items such as mobility aids and identification.

Everyone in the vehicle wears a seat belt. Wheelchairs and other mobility devices are secured according to the equipment's instructions, and the client transfers to a vehicle seat only according to the service plan and transfer technique (SVC-02).
Aides do not use a handheld phone while driving, do not drive while impaired or fatigued, and do not transport more persons than the vehicle has seat belts for.

An aide does not transport a client against the client's or family's wishes. If the client refuses to ride or the aide thinks the trip is unsafe, the aide stops, ensures the client is safe, and calls the Client Care Supervisor.
Aides do not use the transport for personal errands or carry other passengers, such as friends or family, unless the client agrees and the Client Care Supervisor approves.

The aide records each trip in the visit record (SVC-06): date, start and end times, destination, and mileage. Mileage is reimbursed under PER-07 and Labor Code §2802, and charged to the client only as shown in the service agreement (CR-06).

If a client has a medical emergency during transport, the aide pulls over safely, calls 911, then calls the Client Care Supervisor (SVC-07). After any collision, injury, or complaint, the aide reports to the Client Care Supervisor immediately, and the Administrator handles the incident report (SAF-02).

Reasonable modifications for disabled clients, such as extra time or assistance with wheelchair loading, are provided. Service animals are allowed. If a request cannot be met safely, the Client Care Supervisor documents why and suggests an alternative such as paratransit (CR-05).
The Administrator reviews transport records, aide driver files and incidents annually (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether transportation is offered, confirms insurance, and reviews incidents.
Approves drivers, keeps license, insurance and vehicle-check files, and trains aides.
Schedules transport trips only for approved drivers.
Drives safely, secures passengers, keeps trip records and reports problems.

documentation: Aide driver file: license, insurance, safe-vehicle check
Insurance confirmation
Service plan transport authorization
Trip and mileage records
Safe-transport training entries on the log (TRN-05)
Incident reports

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Procedure for Response to Abuse Reporting Duties
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, designee, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, all affiliated home care aides, volunteers and any other person with care or custody responsibility for a client of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To state how [AGENCY NAME] responds when abuse, neglect, abandonment, isolation or financial exploitation of a client is observed, known, suspected or disclosed. This includes who reports, how fast, to whom, and how the Administrator confirms the report, protects the client and keeps a copy of every report available for CDSS review.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 (8/15), p.16, item B5(c) — Program Description element: Procedure for response to abuse reporting duties. [AGENCY NAME] treats every aide and staff member as a mandated reporter. Anyone with full or intermittent responsibility for the care or custody of an elder or dependent adult, whether paid or not, must report observed, known or reasonably suspected physical abuse, abandonment, abduction, isolation, financial abuse or neglect. A report is also required when the client discloses abuse (WIC §15630, C20). Each report is made by telephone or confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible. A written or internet report follows within 2 working days. For abuse in a client's home, the report goes to the county adult protective services (APS) agency or local law enforcement. Suspected child abuse is reported as required by Penal Code §§11164-11174.3 (C10).
