[AGENCY NAME] makes and keeps a copy of EACH suspected-abuse report and makes it available to CDSS during normal business hours (HSC §1796.42(e), C10). CDSS cross-reports abuse reports it receives to local law enforcement and to APS (adult victim) or CPS (child victim) but has no duty to investigate beyond that (HSC §1796.52, C18). A notice to CDSS therefore never replaces the agency's own report to APS, CPS or law enforcement. No one at [AGENCY NAME] may block, delay, discourage, or require supervisor approval for a report. Retaliation against anyone who reports is prohibited.

definitions.definition: A person with full or intermittent responsibility for the care or custody of an elder or dependent adult, paid or unpaid, who must report abuse under WIC §15630. All [AGENCY NAME] aides, staff and volunteers are treated as mandated reporters.
An objectively reasonable belief, based on the facts a person in the same position would hold, that abuse may have occurred. Proof is not required, and the reporter does not investigate.

definitions.term: Physical abuse, abandonment, abduction, isolation, financial abuse, neglect
definitions.definition: The categories of elder and dependent adult mistreatment that must be reported under WIC §15630. Self-neglect and other concerns are also reported to APS.
The county Adult Protective Services agency that receives reports of abuse of elders and dependent adults living outside long-term care facilities.
A normal business day, excluding weekends and holidays, used to count the 2-working-day deadline for the written or internet report.

procedures: Every aide and staff member receives this policy at hire and signs an acknowledgment before client contact. Reporting duties are also taught in entry-level training (see TRN-02) and reviewed at least annually (see TRN-03).
If a client is in immediate danger or needs emergency medical care, the aide calls 911 first, stays with the client if it is safe, and then makes the abuse report.

Any person who observes, knows of, reasonably suspects, or is told by the client about abuse, neglect, abandonment, isolation, abduction or financial exploitation makes the report personally. The duty cannot be delegated and does not depend on a supervisor's agreement.

The reporter telephones, or uses the confidential internet reporting tool of, the county APS agency ([COUNTY APS PHONE]) or local law enforcement ([LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT PHONE]) immediately or as soon as practicably possible. For suspected child abuse, the reporter contacts child protective services or law enforcement under Penal Code §§11164-11174.3.
The reporter sends the written or internet follow-up report within 2 working days of the telephone report, using the form or online tool required by APS, CPS or law enforcement.

The reporter gives the facts only: who, what, when, where, injuries or signs seen, and the client's own words. The reporter does not investigate, interview the client repeatedly, confront the suspected abuser, or promise the client confidentiality.

The reporter then notifies the Client Care Supervisor or Administrator at [PHONE] the same day that a report was made. This is a notice, not a request for permission. If the Administrator or a supervisor is the person suspected, the reporter notifies the licensee, or another designee, instead.

The Administrator, or designee, confirms within 1 working day that the telephone report was made. If the aide did not report, the Administrator makes the report immediately, and the missed duty is handled under PER-09.

The Administrator confirms that the written or internet report was sent within 2 working days. The Administrator obtains a copy from the reporter, or prepares one, and files it in the confidential abuse-report file kept separate from the client's routine service record.

The Administrator acts to protect the client. This includes removing the suspected aide from the client's schedule immediately, arranging a replacement aide, adjusting visit times, and cooperating with the investigating agency. Evidence is preserved, and the client's and reporter's privacy is protected.

If an employee or affiliated aide is the suspect, the Administrator suspends client contact pending the outcome. The Administrator does not interview the client or witnesses in a way that could interfere with the investigation, and does not discuss the report with the suspected person beyond what is needed to remove them from duty. Employment actions follow PER-09, and any separation notice to CDSS follows PER-10.
The Administrator tells the client, and the client's representative if one exists and is not the suspect, that a report was made, unless the investigating agency advises otherwise.

The Administrator sends a copy of the report to CDSS HCSB when CDSS requests it. HCSB: (877) 424-5778, HCSB@dss.ca.gov, 744 P Street, M.S. 9-14-90, Sacramento, CA 95814. The Administrator also understands that CDSS cross-reports to law enforcement and APS or CPS.
The Administrator logs the case in the incident log (see SAF-02) with the date, time, agencies contacted, report copy location, protective actions and follow-up contacts.

The Administrator follows up with APS, CPS or law enforcement as needed, documents each contact and its outcome, and updates the client's service plan or risk measures with the Client Care Supervisor (see SVC-02).
The Administrator reviews every report quarterly in quality assurance (see GOV-05) to identify patterns, training needs or staffing and supervision changes.
The agency keeps each report copy where CDSS can review it during normal business hours and produces it without delay during an inspection (see GOV-07). Retention follows REC-01.

responsibilities.role: Affiliated home care aide / all staff
responsibilities.duty: Report observed, known, suspected or disclosed abuse by phone or confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible; send the written or internet report within 2 working days; notify the supervisor the same day; give a copy to the Administrator.
Receive notices, check that the aide has reported, support the aide, and report personally if the aide has not.
Verify that required reports were made and sent on time, protect the client, keep a copy of each report, document follow-up, make records available to CDSS, and prevent retaliation.
Ensure resources, training and a clear reporting process exist, and act as the reporting contact when the Administrator is involved in the allegation.

documentation: Copy of each telephone-report log entry and written or internet report (kept in the confidential abuse-report file)
Staff and aide acknowledgment of this policy
Incident log entry with protective actions and follow-up contacts
Records of verification by the Administrator within 1 working day (phone) and 2 working days (written)
Records of any CDSS request for report copies and the agency's response

policies.category: B5. Home Care Organization Program Description
policies.title: Service Area — Counties and Areas Served
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, designee, Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, Client Care Supervisor and anyone who accepts clients, schedules aides or advertises for [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define the counties and areas in which [AGENCY NAME] provides non-medical home care, so that intake, scheduling and advertising stay within what the Program Description states and the agency can staff safely.
policies.policy: This policy meets HCS 281 (8/15), p.16, item B5(d) — Program Description element: Description of counties/area where clients are served (attach map if necessary). [AGENCY NAME] provides services only in the following counties and areas: [LIST COUNTIES AND CITIES/ZIP CODES SERVED]. A map of the service area is attached to the Program Description (see PRG-01) when the area cannot be described clearly in words. The agency's license is issued by the CDSS Home Care Services Branch (HCSB), (877) 424-5778. The agency does not accept clients outside the stated service area unless the Program Description has first been updated. The service area is set with aide availability, travel time and mileage cost in mind. Advertising must match the licensed program and the stated service area.

definitions.definition: The counties, cities or ZIP codes listed in the Program Description where [AGENCY NAME] accepts clients and sends aides.
A request for services at an address outside the listed service area.
The document submitted with the HCS 281 application, section B5, describing services, area, hours, population served, and assignment and supervision of aides.

procedures: Before licensure, the licensee and Administrator choose the service area using the number of available aides, typical travel time between clients, aide mileage cost (see PER-07) and the supervisory visit schedule (see SVC-03).
The Administrator lists each county, and any partial-county areas by city or ZIP code, in the Program Description, and attaches a map where needed.
The Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator keeps a one-page service-area list at the intake desk and in the scheduling system.
At first contact, intake staff confirm the client's service address is inside the service area before beginning an assessment (see SVC-01).

If the address is outside the service area, intake staff explain that the agency cannot serve that location. With the client's agreement, they offer referrals to other licensed HCOs or to the county information and referral line.
The agency will not make exceptions for out-of-area clients on a case-by-case basis. The Administrator must first update the Program Description and obtain any needed update on file with CDSS.
Before adding a county or area, the Administrator confirms there are enough qualified aides and a supervisor who can reach the area, and that insurance coverage extends to it (see GOV-03).

The Administrator updates the Program Description and map, records the new version in the document-control log (see GOV-04), and notifies HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov if the change must be reported.
The Administrator removes an area from the list if the agency can no longer staff it safely, and follows SVC-08 for any current clients affected.

Marketing staff review every advertisement, web page and directory listing against this policy and the licensed program. Advertisements name only the licensed service area and non-medical services (see GOV-02).
The Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator checks each new assignment against the service-area list and reports any out-of-area address to the Administrator before the first visit.
The Administrator reviews the service area at least annually, with intake, scheduling and complaint data (see GOV-05), and records the review in the policy review log.

responsibilities.duty: Set, document and update the service area and map; approve any expansion only after the Program Description is revised; ensure advertising matches.
Approve the service area and resources, and keep insurance and licensing records consistent with it.
Verify the address of every new client and assignment against the service-area list; refer out-of-area requests to the Administrator.
Confirm supervisory visits can be made across the service area; report staffing or travel problems.

documentation: Service-area list and map attached to the Program Description
Document-control log entry for every change to the service area
Intake record showing the address check for each inquiry
Out-of-area referral log
Annual service-area review note

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Licensee and Designee Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Licensee, governing body (owners, members, directors and officers), Administrator, HCS 308 designee(s) and management staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed. It sets out who holds ultimate responsibility as licensee, how designees are named, how board members are prepared for their duties, and how ownership records are kept current.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is a Home Care Organization licensed by the CDSS Home Care Services Branch to provide non-medical home care through registered home care aides. The licensee holds ultimate responsibility for compliance with the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act and CDSS requirements. The Act sets no administrator license or registered nurse requirement, so the agency does not claim one. The licensee instead names at least one designee on form HCS 308, as the HCS 281 application requires (C25). A licensee cannot designate him- or herself. A limited liability company or corporation attaches a board resolution to the HCS 308. The licensee must pass the background exam and complete the CDSS orientation (HSC §1796.37(a)(6)-(7), C4). The licensee ensures each board member understands his or her duties (HSC §1796.37(a)(11), C4), and board members sign form HCS 9165 before joining. The agency keeps form HCS 309, which lists owners, members and officers, current. The agency cooperates with CDSS at all times (HSC §1796.37(a)(13), C4).

definitions.definition: The person or legal entity to which CDSS issues the HCO license and that is accountable for the operation of [AGENCY NAME].
A person named in writing by the licensee, other than the licensee, who is authorized to act for the agency, including responding to CDSS and signing required documents.
The owners, members, directors or officers who direct the business. For a sole proprietor, the licensee alone.
[ADMINISTRATOR NAME], the person responsible for day-to-day operation of [AGENCY NAME].

procedures: The licensee completes the CDSS orientation and passes the background exam before licensure, and keeps the completion records on file.

The licensee names at least one designee on HCS 308. The licensee does not list him- or herself as a designee. If the agency is an LLC or corporation, the licensee attaches the board resolution authorizing the designee.
The licensee lists all owners, members and officers on HCS 309 and keeps it current. The Administrator checks the form at each annual policy review and after any change in ownership.

Before a person joins the board or becomes an officer, he or she signs HCS 9165. The licensee reviews the board member's duties with him or her, including the duty to comply with the Act and cooperate with CDSS, and records the date.
The licensee discloses to CDSS any prior role in a licensed facility and any discipline against that role, as the licensing process requires (HSC §1796.37(a)(9)-(10)).

The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], manages day-to-day operations: hiring, scheduling oversight, training, records, client complaints, incident handling and policy compliance. The Administrator reports to the licensee.

The governing body meets at least quarterly, or more often if needed, and keeps written minutes covering compliance, quality assurance results (see GOV-05), complaints, incidents, finances and policy approvals.
The licensee reviews and approves each policy and each revision (see GOV-04) and signs the manual approval page.
The licensee names a new designee in writing before the current designee leaves or is unavailable, so a designee is always available. The Administrator updates HCS 308 and any other CDSS filings.
The licensee reports to CDSS any change of owner, officer, location or corporation as required (see GOV-02) and updates HCS 309 and 9165 as required.

The licensee and Administrator keep the license, application records, HCS 308, HCS 309 and HCS 9165 in a locked governance file at [ADDRESS], and can produce them for any CDSS inspection (see GOV-07).
The licensee reviews this policy at least annually and after any change in the Act or CDSS instructions, and records the review in the document-control log.

responsibilities.duty: Hold ultimate responsibility for compliance; complete orientation and pass the background exam; name a designee other than him- or herself; ensure board members understand their duties; keep ownership records current.
Sign HCS 9165 before joining, understand their duties, oversee compliance and quality assurance, and approve policies.
Manage day-to-day operations, supervise management staff, maintain governance records and cooperate with CDSS.
Act within the authority given on HCS 308, respond to CDSS requests, and notify the licensee of any matter affecting the license.

documentation: Completed HCS 308 and board resolution (if applicable)
Current HCS 309 (owners, members and officers)
Signed HCS 9165 for each board member and record of duties briefing
CDSS orientation completion and background exam records
Governing body minutes and policy approval page
Annual policy review record

policies.title: Licensure, Renewal, Fees, Changes and Advertising
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, designee and any staff who handle licensing filings, fees, marketing or advertising for [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] stays licensed. It covers the 2-year license term, timely renewal and payment of fees, reporting of changes to CDSS, and truthful advertising that matches the licensed program.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only while holding a valid HCO license issued by the CDSS Home Care Services Branch (HCSB). The license term is 2 years. The fee is $5,603 and is non-refundable, and the same fee applies at renewal (HSC §1796.49 and CDSS fee schedule, C16, C26). The renewal fee must be postmarked on or before the license expiration date. CDSS mails a fee notice at least 60 days before the renewal date, but the agency does not wait for that notice and tracks its own date (HSC §1796.37(b)-(c), C4). The agency must have no outstanding fees or civil penalties at renewal (HSC §1796.37(a)(8), C4). A change of location carries a $100 fee and a change in corporation a $200 fee (C26). [AGENCY NAME] provides only non-medical services, as the program description states, and advertises only those services. The HCO license number is displayed in advertising. The agency is an HCO and not an exempt entity such as a licensed home health agency or hospice, an IHSS provider, an employment agency referring independent aides, or a DDS-vendored organization (C3). It does not hold itself out as any of those.

definitions.definition: The license issued by CDSS HCSB allowing [AGENCY NAME] to operate as a Home Care Organization providing non-medical care through registered home care aides.
The date the 2-year license expires. The renewal fee must be postmarked on or before this date.
Moving the agency's office to a new address, which requires notice to CDSS and a $100 fee.
A change in the corporate or entity structure of the licensee, which requires notice to CDSS and a $200 fee.
Services that do not require a licensed health professional, such as companionship, meal preparation and personal care within the scope in PRG-03.

procedures: On receipt of the license, the Administrator enters the license number and expiration date in the compliance calendar and posts the license as required in PRG-02.
The Administrator sets calendar reminders at 180, 120, 90 and 60 days before expiration, with a hard internal deadline for mailing the renewal at least 30 days before the expiration date.

When CDSS mails the fee notice (at least 60 days before the renewal date), the Administrator logs its receipt. If no notice has arrived by 60 days before expiration, the Administrator contacts HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov, and renews on time regardless.
Before renewal, the Administrator confirms there are no outstanding fees or civil penalties, and that insurance, workers' compensation and the bond are in force (see GOV-03).

The Administrator prepares the renewal package, including the $5,603 fee. The package is sent by trackable mail to HCSB, 744 P Street, M.S. 9-14-90, Sacramento, CA 95814, so the postmark date can be proven.
The Administrator keeps a copy of the renewal package, the payment record and the postmark receipt in the licensing file.
Before moving the office, the Administrator notifies HCSB, submits the $100 change-of-location fee with the required forms, and updates the posted license, insurance and advertising.

Before any change in corporation (for example a change in entity type or ownership structure), the licensee notifies HCSB, pays the $200 fee and files the required forms and updated HCS 309 (see GOV-01).
The Administrator reports to CDSS any other change that CDSS instructions require, and records the date, method and confirmation.

The Administrator reviews all advertising, including websites, social media, brochures and directory listings, before use. Advertising describes only the non-medical services the agency is licensed to provide, in the service area stated in PRG-06, and shows the HCO license number.
Advertising must not claim or imply nursing, medical, skilled or hospice services, or any status the agency does not hold. It must not describe the agency as exempt from licensure.
If advertising is found to be inaccurate, the Administrator withdraws or corrects it within 1 business day and records the correction.
The Administrator tracks CDSS correspondence, deficiencies and civil penalties, pays any assessed amount by the due date, and reports status to the licensee at each governing body meeting.

responsibilities.duty: Ensure the license is renewed on time, fees are paid and changes are reported; approve advertising policy.
Maintain the licensing calendar, prepare and mail renewal packages, file change notices, review advertising and keep licensing records.
Use only approved advertising text and display the license number; refer questions about services outside the license to the Administrator.

documentation: Copy of current license and compliance calendar
CDSS fee notice and renewal package copy with postmark proof
Change-of-location and change-in-corporation filings with fee receipts
Advertising review log and approved advertising copies
Record of any civil penalties or outstanding fees and their payment

policies.title: Required Insurance, Workers' Compensation and Employee Dishonesty Bond
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, designee and any staff who maintain insurance or bond records for [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] always carries the general and professional liability insurance, workers' compensation and employee dishonesty bond that the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act requires, and can prove it to CDSS.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains, without lapse: (1) general and professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate (HSC §1796.42(d), C9); (2) a valid workers' compensation policy covering affiliated aides (HSC §1796.42(b), C7); and (3) an employee dishonesty bond, including third-party coverage, of at least $10,000 (HSC §1796.42(c), C8). The bond is documented on form HCS 402, which names the State of California as beneficiary. Licensure requires proof of each coverage, with the workers' compensation policy number, dates, and carrier name and address (HSC §1796.37(a)(2)-(4), C4). The agency gives certificates to CDSS on request. A lapse in any coverage violates operating requirements, so renewals are calendared and tracked.

definitions.definition: Insurance covering claims of bodily injury, property damage and professional errors arising from the agency's services, at not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate.
Insurance that covers work-related injury and illness of the agency's affiliated aides and other employees.

A bond of at least $10,000, including third-party coverage, protecting clients and others against theft or dishonest acts by the agency's employees. Form HCS 402 names the State of California as beneficiary.
A document from the carrier showing the type of coverage, limits, policy number, effective dates and insured entity.

procedures: Before applying for licensure, the licensee obtains the three required coverages from carriers authorized to write them in California, with limits at or above the minimums in this policy.
The Administrator obtains a certificate of insurance for the liability policy that shows $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate and covers both general and professional liability.
The Administrator records the workers' compensation policy number, effective dates, carrier name and carrier address, and confirms the policy covers all affiliated aides.
The licensee obtains the $10,000 employee dishonesty bond with third-party coverage and completes form HCS 402 naming the State of California as beneficiary.
The Administrator files all certificates, policies and the HCS 402 in the insurance file at [ADDRESS] and submits copies to CDSS as part of the application.
The Administrator enters each policy and bond expiration date in the compliance calendar, with reminders at 90, 60 and 30 days before expiration.
At least 30 days before each expiration date, the Administrator confirms renewal with the carrier or broker and obtains the new certificate before the old coverage ends.
The Administrator checks that the aides' pay is correctly reported for workers' compensation purposes and that the number of aides matches the carrier's records at each audit.

If any coverage is cancelled, non-renewed or reduced, the Administrator notifies the licensee the same day. The licensee replaces it without a gap and the Administrator notifies CDSS HCSB at (877) 424-5778 if the lapse affects compliance.

The agency does not allow aides to provide services during any period in which a required coverage is not in force. The licensee decides whether to suspend services and notifies clients as appropriate.
The Administrator provides certificates to CDSS promptly when requested and keeps a record of each request and response.

The Administrator reviews coverage amounts, exclusions and claims history with the licensee at least annually, and reports claims or injuries to the carrier within the carrier's reporting period (see SAF-02 and SAF-05).
The Administrator reports the status of all three coverages to the governing body at each meeting (see GOV-01).

responsibilities.duty: Purchase and keep in force all three coverages at or above required limits; approve renewals; replace any lapsed coverage immediately.
Maintain the insurance file, track expiration dates, obtain certificates, report claims and give proof to CDSS on request.
Provide accurate aide counts and payroll data for workers' compensation audits.

documentation: Certificates of insurance for liability coverage
Workers' compensation policy number, dates, carrier name and address
Employee dishonesty bond and HCS 402
Compliance calendar showing expiration and renewal dates
Records of claims, carrier notices and CDSS requests for proof

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, designee, supervisors and all staff who use or maintain the [AGENCY NAME] Policy and Procedure Manual
policies.purpose: To make sure the manual is reviewed regularly, kept accurate, controlled by version, and consistent with the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act and with the personnel policies and training plan on file with CDSS.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] reviews the entire manual at least annually and also reviews it after any change in the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (HSC §1796.10 et seq., C1) or in CDSS instructions. This is the agency's own operating standard. Every policy shows its version, effective date and approver. The agency updates the personnel policies and training plan it has on file with CDSS whenever they change, since the application requires them (HCS 281 items B3 and B4, C25). The known pending change is dementia training for aides, effective January 1, 2027, which is addressed in TRN-04. Superseded versions are retired with the retirement date and kept as a record.

definitions.definition: A policy, form or plan in the manual that carries a version number, effective date and approver and may be changed only through this policy.
A policy version replaced by a newer approved version. It is marked with the retirement date and removed from use.
The log that records each policy's ID, title, version, effective date, approver, review date and any retired versions.

procedures: The Administrator maintains one master copy of the manual, in electronic and printed form, at [ADDRESS]. Only the master copy is current.
Each policy page shows the policy ID, title, version number, effective date and approver. New policies start at version 1.0 on the date the licensee approves them.
The Administrator keeps the document-control log listing every policy, its current version, last review date and next review date.

At least annually, the Administrator and the Client Care Supervisor review every policy against current practice, incidents, complaints, inspection results and quality assurance findings (see GOV-05), and record the review date for each policy.

The Administrator checks the text of the Act and CDSS instructions at least annually, and at any time the agency learns of a change, and revises affected policies within 30 days of learning of the change.

The Administrator tracks known pending changes. The Administrator has calendared the January 1, 2027 effective date for dementia training and will approve the revised training plan before that date (see TRN-01, TRN-03 and TRN-04).
Anyone may propose a policy change in writing to the Administrator, stating the policy ID, the reason and the suggested wording.
The Administrator drafts the revision, marks the changes, gets the Client Care Supervisor's input where services or supervision are affected, and sends the revision to the licensee.
The licensee approves the revision by signing and dating it. The version number and effective date are updated, and the change is recorded in the document-control log.
When a revision changes the personnel policies (HCS 281 item B3) or the training plan (item B4), the Administrator updates the copy on file with CDSS and keeps proof of the update.
The Administrator distributes the revised policy to all affected staff within 7 days of approval, trains them on the change, and collects signed acknowledgments in the personnel or training file.
On the effective date of a new version, the Administrator removes the superseded version from the working manual, marks it 'SUPERSEDED' with the retirement date, and files it in the archive.
The Administrator keeps superseded versions long enough to show what policy was in force on any date, and in line with REC-01.

The Administrator keeps the manual available to CDSS during inspections (see GOV-07) and to staff at all times. Clients receive the policies that concern their rights and complaints as set out in CR-01 and CR-02.

responsibilities.duty: Approve every policy and revision; ensure annual review occurs and the manual reflects current law.
Maintain the master manual and document-control log, run annual and change-driven reviews, update items on file with CDSS and train staff on revisions.
Review service and supervision policies, report practice gaps and help train staff on changes.
Use only the current version, sign acknowledgments of revisions and report policy problems to the Administrator.

documentation: Master manual with version, effective date and approver on each policy
Document-control log with annual review dates
Signed approval pages and revision drafts
Archive of superseded versions marked with retirement date
Staff acknowledgments of revised policies
Proof of updated personnel policies and training plan on file with CDSS

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, and all affiliated home care aides
policies.purpose: To establish a documented, recurring process through which [AGENCY NAME] measures the quality and safety of its non-medical home care services, finds problems early, corrects them, and reports results to the licensee so that the agency stays in compliance with the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (HSC §1796.10 et seq.) and its own policies.
policies.policy: The Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (HSC §1796.10 et seq.) does not prescribe a quality assurance program. [AGENCY NAME] therefore adopts this policy as an operator standard. No checklist item is assigned to this policy. [AGENCY NAME] will run a Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QA/PI) program that reviews incidents, complaints, missed visits and supervisory-visit findings at least quarterly. It will also track each aide's registry status, tuberculosis (TB) screening due dates and training hours, track client satisfaction, and track corrective actions to completion. The Administrator will report QA/PI results to the licensee (and governing body, if one exists) every quarter. Findings that show a risk to client safety are acted on immediately and are not held until the next quarterly review.

definitions.definition: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement: the agency's routine process for measuring performance, identifying problems and carrying out corrective action.
A specific, countable measure reviewed each quarter, such as the number of missed visits or the percentage of aides with current TB documentation.
A written plan that names the problem, the cause, the action to be taken, the person responsible and the due date.

Any event involving serious harm or a risk of serious harm to a client or aide, or any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation. It is escalated immediately under SAF-02 and PRG-05 and is also reviewed in QA/PI.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], leads the QA/PI program. By January 31 of each year the Administrator appoints a QA/PI review team of the Administrator, the Client Care Supervisor and the Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator. The licensee may attend.
The team meets at least once each calendar quarter (by April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31 for the preceding quarter). The Administrator keeps meeting minutes with attendees and the date.

Before each meeting the Administrator collects the incident log (SAF-02) and counts incidents by type, client, aide and location. The Administrator also looks for trends such as repeated falls or the same aide appearing in several reports.
The Administrator collects the complaint log (CR-02) and reviews the number of complaints, the time to acknowledgement and resolution, the substantiated rate and any repeat complainants.

The Scheduler reports missed, late and cancelled visits (SVC-05) and EVV or timekeeping exceptions (SVC-06). The report shows the cause of each (aide, client, scheduling, transportation) and whether replacement coverage was arranged.
The Client Care Supervisor reports the supervisory visits (SVC-03) completed against those due, the findings from each visit, and the service plan updates (SVC-02) made as a result.

The Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator produces a compliance roster for every affiliated aide. It shows registry clearance and registration expiration (PER-03, PER-04), TB screening date and next due date (PER-05), entry-level training completed before client contact (TRN-02), annual training hours (TRN-03), and dementia training status once required (TRN-04, effective January 1, 2027). Any gap is corrected before the aide is scheduled again.

The Client Care Supervisor sends or conducts a client satisfaction survey at least every six months and after discharge. The survey is available in the client's preferred language (CR-05). Responses are tallied and any dissatisfied respondent is called within 5 business days.

The team compares each indicator with the prior quarter and with the agency targets: 100% of aides cleared on the registry before client contact, 100% of aides with current TB documentation and training, 100% of supervisory visits completed on schedule, and no missed visit left without replacement coverage or client notice.

For every indicator below target, the team writes a corrective action plan that states the cause, the action, the responsible person and a due date no later than the next quarterly meeting. For a client-safety issue the Administrator acts the same day.

The Administrator tracks open corrective actions on a CAP log and reviews them at each meeting. An action is closed only when evidence of completion is attached, and the team confirms the fix worked at the next review.
Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation are never held for QA review. They are handled under PRG-05 and SAF-01 and are listed in QA/PI only after the report has been made.

Within 15 days after each quarterly meeting the Administrator gives the licensee a written QA/PI report with the indicators, trends, corrective actions and open items. The licensee signs and dates it to show review.

The Administrator prepares an annual QA/PI summary each January. It recommends changes to policies, training, staffing or scheduling, which are routed through GOV-04 (Policy Review and Document Control).
QA/PI reports are kept with the administrative records, are available to CDSS inspectors (GOV-07), and contain client and aide identifiers only as needed. Client details are protected under CR-03.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews and signs the quarterly QA/PI report, provides resources for corrective actions and acts on recommendations.
Leads the QA/PI team, compiles the incident and complaint data, writes corrective action plans, tracks them to closure and issues the quarterly and annual reports.
Reports supervisory-visit findings and client satisfaction results, and follows up on dissatisfied clients and service plan changes.
Reports missed visits and EVV exceptions and maintains the aide compliance roster for registry, TB and training.
Report incidents and concerns promptly, complete required training and cooperate with corrective actions.

documentation: QA/PI team appointment and quarterly meeting minutes
Quarterly QA/PI indicator report signed by the licensee
Incident, complaint and missed-visit summaries
Aide compliance roster (registry, TB due date, training hours)
Client satisfaction survey results and follow-up notes
Corrective action plan (CAP) log with completion evidence
Annual QA/PI summary

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, Client Care Supervisor, and all affiliated home care aides
policies.purpose: To ensure that [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered within the scope of non-medical home care, protects client funds and payer funds from fraud, waste and abuse, and avoids the license consequences described in HSC §1796.38.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will bill only for hours actually worked by an aide in the client's presence. It will bill only for services within the scope of home care services described in its program description and in PRG-03. Electronic visit verification (EVV) is required for Medicaid-funded personal care services under 42 U.S.C. §1396b(l). It applies only to Medi-Cal-funded visits, and the agency will confirm the required EVV system with the Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) or the contracting managed care plan before billing any Medi-Cal-funded visit. Personal Care and Homemaker Services (PCHS) under Medi-Cal managed care Community Supports are offered by plans, which contract with and pay providers; the agency will follow the compliance program, exclusion screening and billing terms in each plan contract (DHCS Community Supports Policy Guide, Vol. 1). The agency will keep its employee dishonesty bond in force at all times, in at least the amount required for licensure of $10,000 including third-party coverage (see GOV-03). Violations of this policy may result in discipline, repayment, referral to authorities and action against the license under HSC §1796.38 (denial, suspension or revocation). No checklist item is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: Knowingly billing or causing a bill for services not delivered, hours not worked, or services outside the agency's scope, or otherwise deceiving a client or payer to obtain payment.
Practices that result in unnecessary cost or improper payment even without clear intent, such as rounding hours up or poor documentation.

Electronic visit verification: an electronic record of the service type, the individual receiving and the individual providing the service, the date, the location, and the start and end times of a visit. EVV is required for Medicaid personal care services.
Checking staff and the agency against the exclusion or suspension lists that a payer contract requires, before hire and periodically afterward.
The person designated by the licensee to oversee this policy. Until another person is named, the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], serves in this role.

procedures: The licensee designates a Compliance Officer in writing. The Compliance Officer reports directly to the licensee on compliance matters and has access to all billing, payroll and visit records.

Billing is based on the verified time record for each visit: EVV data for Medi-Cal-funded visits, and the timekeeping record under SVC-06 for all other visits. The Billing Coordinator may not bill for scheduled time that was not worked.

Before the first Medi-Cal-funded visit under any plan or program, the Billing Coordinator confirms in writing with DHCS or the managed care plan which EVV system is required and sets it up. EVV is not applied to private-pay visits as a legal requirement, though the agency may use the same system for them.

Before billing begins under any managed care plan, the Administrator reads the plan contract for compliance program, exclusion screening, record, audit and claims requirements. The Administrator keeps a summary of those obligations in the compliance file.

The Billing Coordinator reconciles each invoice against visit records, the service plan (SVC-02) and the service agreement and rates (CR-06) before it is sent. Variances are corrected, and a variance over one hour per client per pay period is reviewed by the Administrator.

The agency does not bill for any task outside the scope of home care services (see PRG-03). Examples are medical or nursing tasks, tasks the aide may not lawfully perform, and services never provided. A supervisor who learns of out-of-scope work stops the work and the Billing Coordinator removes it from the bill.

The agency bills clients and plans only at the rates in the service agreement or the plan contract. DHCS pricing benchmarks are non-binding and are used only for negotiation. The agency never charges a client more than the agreed rate or adds undisclosed fees.

Aides record their actual start and end times at the client's home each visit, and may not clock in for another person or from another location. An aide who falsifies a time record or visit note is subject to discipline up to termination (PER-09) and is reported as required.

The Scheduler reviews EVV and timekeeping exceptions (late clock-in, manual edits, missing clock-outs) weekly. Every manual edit requires a written reason and supervisor approval, and the exception log is kept.

Before hire, and at least annually thereafter, the Administrator screens each employee and the agency itself against any exclusion lists named in the plan contract or required by a payer. Screening results are kept in the compliance file (PER-04, PER-06). An excluded person is not hired or retained in a role paid by that payer.

The agency keeps the employee dishonesty bond (including third-party coverage, at least $10,000) in force. The Administrator verifies renewal at least 30 days before expiration and files the proof (GOV-03).

Any employee who suspects a billing error or fraud reports it to the Compliance Officer or the licensee by phone, email or in person. A report may be made anonymously. A person who reports in good faith will not suffer retaliation.

The Compliance Officer opens a file within 2 business days of a report, investigates, preserves records and documents the outcome. A confirmed overbilling is corrected and repaid to the client or payer within the time the contract or applicable law requires. The Compliance Officer decides, with the licensee, whether outside counsel or a government referral is needed.

The Compliance Officer provides compliance training to all billing and scheduling staff and covers billing integrity and the reporting channel in aide orientation (TRN-02) and refreshers. Attendance is logged (TRN-05).
The Compliance Officer includes billing error rates, exception counts, overpayments and fraud reports in the quarterly QA/PI report (GOV-05).

The licensee understands that substantiated fraud, falsified records or misrepresentation can result in denial, suspension or revocation of the license under HSC §1796.38. The licensee and Administrator will cooperate fully with CDSS under GOV-07.

Record accurate time and care notes, perform only in-scope tasks and report suspected fraud.

policies.title: CDSS Inspections and Complaint Investigations
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, designated inspection contact, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, and all office staff
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is ready for random, unannounced inspections by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Home Care Services Branch (HCSB), cooperates fully with complaint investigations, and never obstructs access to books, records or premises.
policies.policy: CDSS verifies Home Care Organization compliance through random, unannounced inspections, and may investigate complaints (HSC §1796.52; HSC §1796.51). Inspections may cover books, records and premises, and refusing access is cause for revocation of the license (HSC §1796.52). CDSS may enter the Home Care Organization during posted business hours, with or without advance notice (HSC §1796.53). [AGENCY NAME] will therefore keep its office staffed during posted business hours (PRG-02), designate a staff member to receive inspectors, and keep all required records readily accessible. The agency will cooperate courteously and completely with CDSS, will not retaliate against anyone who files a complaint or speaks with an inspector, and will correct deficiencies promptly. No checklist item is assigned to this policy. CDSS has no oversight of individual registered aides other than maintaining the registry; the agency remains responsible for supervising its aides.

definitions.definition: The Home Care Services Branch of the CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, which licenses Home Care Organizations, maintains the Home Care Aide Registry and conducts inspections and complaint investigations. Phone (877) 424-5778; email HCSB@dss.ca.gov.
A visit by CDSS staff without prior notice, to verify compliance with the Act.
The staff member named to greet inspectors and coordinate access. This is [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] or, in that person's absence, the named alternate.
The hours posted with the license at the office under PRG-02. CDSS may enter during these hours.

procedures: The licensee names the Administrator as the designated inspection contact and one alternate who is on site during posted business hours. Their names are posted at the front desk and in the staff handbook.

All office staff are trained at hire and annually to do the following when someone says they are from CDSS: greet them politely, ask for identification, and immediately call the designated contact. Staff do not turn inspectors away or ask them to come back later.

The designated contact verifies the inspector's CDSS identification, notes the name and the time of arrival, and invites the inspector into a private space. The licensee is notified by phone as soon as possible. The inspection is not delayed while waiting for the licensee.

The agency keeps these records in the office and retrievable within minutes: the license, the policy and procedure manual, personnel files (including registry clearance, registration, TB documentation and training records), the training verification log, client records and service agreements, complaint and incident logs, insurance and bond certificates, and QA/PI reports.

During the inspection the designated contact provides every record requested and allows access to the premises. If a record is stored electronically, staff display or print it. Records are not hidden, altered, backdated or removed.

If the inspector asks to speak with an employee or client, the designated contact arranges it. Staff may answer truthfully. Staff are told that nobody may be disciplined for speaking with an inspector.
The designated contact keeps a log of what records were reviewed and what copies were taken, and takes notes of the inspector's questions and comments.

If a requested record is not immediately available, the designated contact tells the inspector when it will be produced, and gives it that same day when possible. Access is never refused. The Administrator tells the licensee that refusing access is cause for revocation of the license (HSC §1796.52).

At the exit conference the designated contact and, when available, the licensee listen to the findings. They ask for clarification of any cited requirement and obtain a copy of any report or deficiency notice left by CDSS.
Within 1 business day after the inspection the Administrator writes an internal summary of what was reviewed, findings and follow-up items, and gives it to the licensee.

For each deficiency the Administrator writes a corrective action plan that states the cause, the action, the person responsible and the due date. The plan is completed within the deadline set by CDSS, or sooner, and the response is delivered to HCSB in writing. The Administrator keeps proof of correction.

When CDSS notifies the agency of a complaint investigation (HSC §§1796.51-.52), the Administrator preserves all related client, aide, schedule, EVV and supervisory records and tells staff not to alter or discard them. The Administrator also notifies the licensee and, if appropriate, the insurer.

The agency cooperates with the investigator, provides requested documents and arranges interviews. The Administrator responds to written findings by the deadline given, and no one retaliates against the complainant, the client or any witness (CR-02).
If an allegation of abuse, neglect or exploitation is involved, the agency also follows PRG-05 and SAF-01 and does not wait for CDSS before making required reports.

The Administrator logs every inspection and complaint investigation (date, inspector, scope, findings, corrective actions, outcome). The log is included in the quarterly QA/PI report (GOV-05). Staff conduct a mock inspection at least once a year to test readiness.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the agency is open and staffed during posted hours, supports prompt access and approves corrective actions.
Receives inspectors, verifies identification, produces records, attends the exit conference and submits corrective action plans.
Greet inspectors courteously and notify the designated contact immediately; never refuse access.
Makes client records and supervisory visit documentation available and assists with corrective actions on service delivery.
Produces schedule, timekeeping, billing and aide registry/TB/training records on request.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All clients and their representatives; Administrator, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler, and all affiliated home care aides
policies.purpose: To state the rights every client of [AGENCY NAME] has, the responsibilities clients are asked to share, and the steps staff take to inform clients of both and to protect those rights.
policies.policy: The Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (HSC §1796.10 et seq.) does not contain a list of client rights, so [AGENCY NAME] adopts this client rights statement as an operator standard. Because annual aide training must cover clients' rights and safety (HSC §1796.44(c)), every aide receives training on this policy. Each client has the right to be treated with dignity and respect; to make informed choices about the care received; to be free from abuse, neglect and exploitation; and to privacy and confidentiality. The agency gives each client or representative a written rights statement at intake and obtains a signature acknowledging receipt. The statement tells the client how to contact the CDSS Home Care Services Branch (HCSB) at (877) 424-5778. No checklist item is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: A person who receives or has applied to receive non-medical home care from [AGENCY NAME].
A person legally authorized to act for the client, such as an agent under a power of attorney, a conservator or a parent or guardian of a minor. The agency asks for proof of the authority.
The client's right to understand the services, rates, risks and alternatives and to accept or refuse services.
Taking or misusing a client's money, property or trust. See CR-04 and SAF-01.

procedures: At intake (SVC-01), before services begin, the Client Care Supervisor reviews the Client Rights and Responsibilities statement with the client or representative, in the client's preferred language or with an interpreter (CR-05), and answers questions.

The client or representative signs and dates the acknowledgment, receives a copy, and the original is placed in the client record (REC-01). If the client cannot sign, the supervisor notes the reason and the name of a witness.

The rights statement tells each client that they have the right to: (a) be treated with dignity, courtesy and respect, and to have their culture, beliefs and home respected; (b) receive care without discrimination (CR-05); (c) be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation and from physical or chemical restraint; (d) privacy in personal care and confidentiality of their information (CR-03); and (e) know the aide's name and that the aide is a registered home care aide.

The statement also says clients have the right to: (a) be told in writing, before services begin, of services, rates, billing and the terms of the service agreement (CR-06) and of changes with advance notice; (b) take part in developing and changing their service plan (SVC-02) and to refuse or stop any service; (c) have their property treated carefully (CR-04); and (d) receive advance written notice of discharge or transfer and reasons (SVC-08).

The statement tells clients they may complain to the agency at any time without retaliation (CR-02), and may contact CDSS HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov. The agency's own phone number [PHONE] and the Administrator's name [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] are also given.

The statement lists client responsibilities, which are to: give accurate information about needs and health conditions; tell the agency of changes in condition, hospitalizations or address; provide a reasonably safe home environment for the aide; treat aides with courtesy and without harassment or discrimination; give notice of cancellations as set in the service agreement; pay for services as agreed; and not ask aides to do work outside the service plan or scope (PRG-03).

Failure to meet client responsibilities does not remove a client's rights. If a responsibility is not met, the Client Care Supervisor first tries to resolve it with the client; discontinuation follows SVC-08 only as a last resort.
The agency posts a copy of the rights statement in the office and gives a copy to any client or family member who asks at any time.

Aides are trained on client rights and safety in orientation (TRN-02) and every year in the annual training (TRN-03; HSC §1796.44(c)). Completion is recorded in the training verification log (TRN-05).

Aides must respect the rights in every visit: introducing themselves, asking permission before providing personal care, closing doors and curtains, and honoring a client's decision to decline a task. They tell the supervisor when a client declines care.

A staff member who sees or hears of a violation of a client's right reports it to the Client Care Supervisor the same day. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported immediately under PER-02 and PRG-05.

During supervisory visits (SVC-03), the Client Care Supervisor asks the client directly whether their rights are being respected, whether they know how to complain and whether they feel safe, and documents the answers.
The Client Care Supervisor re-issues the rights statement when it changes and at each annual service plan review, and records the date given.
Rights violations, complaints about rights and client feedback are summarized quarterly in QA/PI (GOV-05). Any change to this policy follows GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the rights statement, ensures it is accurate and includes CDSS HCSB contact information, and corrects violations.
Reviews the rights statement at intake, obtains the signature, checks rights during supervisory visits and follows up on violations.
Ensures that the rights acknowledgment is on file before the first visit is scheduled.
Complete rights training, respect clients' rights at every visit and report violations or suspected abuse right away.

Interpreter or translation notes when used

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All clients, client representatives and family members; Administrator, Client Care Supervisor, Scheduler, and all affiliated home care aides
policies.purpose: To give clients and their representatives a clear, written way to raise complaints about [AGENCY NAME] or its aides, to make sure each complaint is acknowledged, investigated and resolved promptly and without retaliation, and to tell clients how to contact CDSS.
policies.policy: CDSS may investigate complaints against Home Care Organizations (HSC §1796.51; HSC §1796.52). [AGENCY NAME] gives every client, at intake, a written complaint process and the contact information of the CDSS Home Care Services Branch (HCSB@dss.ca.gov; (877) 424-5778). As an operator standard, the agency acknowledges each complaint in writing within 2 business days and resolves it, with a written response, within 14 calendar days. No client, family member, aide or other person will be retaliated against for making a complaint. Every complaint is logged and reviewed in the quality assurance process (GOV-05). Clients may complain to CDSS at any time, whether or not they have used the agency's process first. No checklist item is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: Any oral or written expression of dissatisfaction about services, staff conduct, billing, privacy, safety or the agency's actions, whether or not the person calls it a complaint.
The client, representative, family member, aide or any other person who raises the concern.
Any adverse action against a person for complaining, such as reducing or ending services, changing the aide as a penalty, or threatening, or disciplining an employee who reports.
A complaint for which the investigation found evidence that the concern was true.

procedures: At intake (SVC-01), the Client Care Supervisor gives the client or representative the written complaint process, explains it, and records that it was given. The document lists the agency contact, [PHONE] and [ADDRESS], the Administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], and the CDSS HCSB contact: (877) 424-5778 and HCSB@dss.ca.gov.

The process tells clients they may complain by phone, in writing, by email or in person, in their preferred language (CR-05), and that a family member or other person may complain on their behalf. Staff help a client write a complaint if requested.

Any employee who receives a complaint, including an aide, writes down the complaint, who made it, the date and the details, and gives it to the Client Care Supervisor or Administrator by the end of the next business day. Staff may not discourage, ignore or argue with the complainant.

If the complaint alleges abuse, neglect or exploitation, the employee tells the supervisor or Administrator immediately and the matter is handled under PER-02, PRG-05 and SAF-01. A report to the proper authorities is not delayed for the grievance process. Complaints that involve an injury or a serious event are also logged under SAF-02.
The Administrator logs each complaint in the complaint log within 1 business day, with a number, date, complainant, client, aide involved, nature, severity and the person assigned to investigate.

Within 2 business days of receipt, the Administrator or Client Care Supervisor sends a written acknowledgment (letter, email or hand-delivered note) that states the date received, who is handling it and when to expect a response.

If the complaint involves a particular aide, the Client Care Supervisor first makes sure the client is safe and comfortable. This may include temporary reassignment at the client's request. Reassignment is not used as a penalty to the client.

The investigator (not the person complained about) interviews the complainant, the aide, other staff and others as appropriate, and reviews schedules, EVV or timekeeping records, notes and the service plan. Findings are written down.

Within 14 calendar days of receipt, the Administrator sends the complainant a written response that states what was found, what was done and any corrective steps, and tells the complainant they may contact CDSS HCSB if not satisfied. If more time is needed, the Administrator sends a written update before day 14 with a new date.

If the complaint is substantiated, the Administrator takes corrective action: retraining, coaching, discipline under PER-09, billing credit (CR-06), or changes to the service plan. Action is documented in the complaint file.
The agency does not retaliate. The Administrator reminds staff of this at the start of each investigation. Any retaliation is itself a policy violation and results in discipline under PER-09.
Complaint information is kept confidential and shared only with people who need it to investigate and resolve it (CR-03).

The Administrator closes the complaint log entry when the response has been sent and the corrective action has been completed. The complete file is kept in the administrative records for the retention period in REC-01.
When CDSS contacts the agency about a complaint, the Administrator follows GOV-07, preserves all related records and cooperates fully.
The Administrator reports complaint numbers, types, time to resolution, substantiation rates and trends every quarter in QA/PI (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Owns the complaint process, keeps the log, ensures acknowledgment and resolution deadlines are met, and prevents retaliation.
Gives the complaint process at intake, receives and investigates complaints, protects the client's safety and follows up with the client.
Logs billing and scheduling complaints and provides records for investigation.
Report every complaint they hear to a supervisor by the next business day, and cooperate with investigations.

Complaint log
Written acknowledgment letters or emails
Investigation notes and findings
Written response to the complainant
Corrective action documentation
Quarterly complaint summary for QA/PI

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: Licensee, Administrator, all staff, volunteers, and affiliated home care aides who have contact with clients, prospective clients or confidential client information
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy and confidentiality of client information held by [AGENCY NAME], to make sure only background-cleared people have access to it, and to set out the steps for compliance with HIPAA where it applies and for responding to a breach.
policies.policy: Any staff person, volunteer or employee who has contact with clients, prospective clients or confidential client information must satisfy the clearance requirements of HSC §1796.43(a)(1) before that contact or access begins (see PER-04). [AGENCY NAME] will determine whether it is a HIPAA covered entity or a business associate (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164), for example because it bills health plans electronically, and will follow HIPAA where it applies. If the agency is a covered entity, it gives each client a Notice of Privacy Practices. In every case, the agency applies the minimum-necessary standard, secures paper and electronic records, uses and discloses client information only as permitted, and follows the breach response steps in this policy. Where the agency is not covered by HIPAA, it nevertheless follows this policy as an operator standard. No checklist item is assigned to this policy.

definitions.definition: Any information that identifies a client or relates to the client's health, care, finances, home, schedule or family, in any form, including oral, paper and electronic.
Individually identifiable health information that is covered by HIPAA when held by a covered entity or business associate.

Terms defined in 45 CFR Part 160. A covered entity includes a health care provider that conducts certain transactions electronically (such as billing health plans). A business associate performs services for a covered entity involving PHI.
Using, disclosing or requesting only the information needed for a task.
An acquisition, access, use or disclosure of confidential client information not permitted by this policy or the law that compromises its privacy or security.

procedures: Before any person is given access to clients or confidential client information, the Administrator confirms that clearance is complete under PER-04 and HSC §1796.43(a)(1), and that the person is registered as required for aides (PER-03). A person who has not been cleared does not enter client homes, see client files, or use scheduling or billing systems.

Within the first 30 days of operation and whenever its billing arrangements change, the Administrator determines in writing whether the agency is a HIPAA covered entity (for example, it bills Medi-Cal managed care plans or other payers electronically) or a business associate of a plan. The determination and its basis are kept in the compliance file.

If the agency is a covered entity, the Administrator adopts the HIPAA privacy and security requirements of 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164 and designates a privacy officer in writing; until another person is named, this is [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. If the agency is a business associate, the Administrator signs and keeps the business associate agreement with each plan.

If the agency is a covered entity, the Client Care Supervisor gives each client or representative the Notice of Privacy Practices at the first service delivery, asks for a signed acknowledgment of receipt, and posts the notice in the office and on any agency website. If the client refuses to sign, the reason is documented.

The Client Care Supervisor obtains a written authorization before disclosing client information, except as allowed or required by law. Examples are reporting suspected abuse (PER-02, PRG-05), an emergency, an audit or inspection by CDSS (GOV-07) or a request from the client. Authorizations are kept in the client record.

Staff access only the information they need for their jobs (minimum necessary). Aides see only the clients they serve. Billing staff see billing and service data. Each user has an individual login. Passwords are not shared.

Aides do not discuss clients with anyone not involved in the client's care, and do not post anything about a client, the client's home or other clients on social media or messaging platforms (PER-08). Photographs of clients may be taken only with written permission and an agency purpose.

Paper client records are kept in locked cabinets in a locked office. Aides do not leave client records in vehicles or public places. Records an aide keeps in the home, such as the service plan, remain in the home.

Electronic records and apps (scheduling, EVV, billing, email) are protected by passwords, automatic log-off, up-to-date software, encryption of devices and secure transmission. Client information is not sent through personal, unsecured email or text. The Administrator disables access for an employee on the day of separation (PER-10).
Computers, phones and paper are securely disposed of or wiped when no longer needed, and not before the records retention period in REC-01 ends.
All staff and aides complete confidentiality and privacy training at hire (TRN-02) and each year (TRN-03) and sign a confidentiality agreement, kept in the personnel file (PER-06).

Any employee who learns of a possible breach (lost device, misdirected message, unauthorized access, discussion in public) reports it to the Administrator immediately and no later than the end of the same day.
The Administrator takes steps to contain the breach (retrieving or deleting information, disabling access, changing passwords) and opens a breach file within 1 business day.

The Administrator assesses what was involved, who accessed it, whether the information was actually viewed or used, and the risk of harm, and decides whether notification is required. If the agency is a covered entity or business associate, notification follows the breach notification requirements of 45 CFR Part 164 and any applicable California law, and any plan contract deadlines. Notice goes to affected clients in writing without unreasonable delay, and to others as required.

The Administrator documents the investigation, notifications and corrective actions (retraining, discipline under PER-09, system changes), keeps the breach file for the retention period in REC-01, and reports breaches in QA/PI (GOV-05).

Clients may ask to see or get a copy of their records, ask for corrections and ask who the information has been shared with. The Client Care Supervisor handles each request in writing and replies within the time that applicable law or the plan contract requires, or within 30 days if none applies.

responsibilities.duty: Provides resources for safeguards, ensures a privacy officer is designated and supports corrective action after a breach.
Confirms clearance before access, determines HIPAA status, signs business associate agreements, oversees safeguards, investigates breaches and handles notifications.
Gives the Notice of Privacy Practices when required, gets authorizations and handles client requests about records.
Limits access to systems by role, manages user accounts and secures billing and scheduling information.

responsibilities.role: Affiliated Home Care Aides and all staff
responsibilities.duty: Keep client information confidential, access only what is needed, protect records and devices and report any suspected breach the same day.

documentation: Clearance confirmation before access (PER-04)
HIPAA covered entity or business associate determination
Privacy officer designation and business associate agreements
Notice of Privacy Practices and signed acknowledgments, if a covered entity
Client authorizations for disclosure
Signed staff confidentiality agreements
Privacy training records
Breach log, investigation file and notifications
User access list and account deactivation records

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] affiliated home care aides, the Client Care Supervisor, the Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator, the Administrator and designee, the licensee, and volunteers
policies.purpose: To protect clients from theft, undue influence and financial abuse, and to make sure any suspected financial exploitation of an elder or dependent adult is reported within the time limits in WIC §15630.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides non-medical home care and does not manage clients' money or property. Financial abuse of an elder or dependent adult is reportable under WIC §15630. Persons with full or intermittent responsibility for the care of an elder or dependent adult, paid or unpaid, are mandated reporters. [AGENCY NAME] treats every aide, supervisor, scheduler, administrator and volunteer as a mandated reporter for this purpose. As an operator standard, no staff member may accept gifts, loans, bequests or appointments as agent under a power of attorney from a client or the client's family, or be named in a client's will or trust. Aides do not take or use a client's bank cards, credit cards or PINs. Whenever an aide handles cash for shopping or errands, a written receipt is required. Suspected financial exploitation is reported within the abuse-reporting timelines: by telephone or confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible, with a written or internet report within 2 working days. For abuse outside a long-term care facility, the report goes to the county adult protective services agency or local law enforcement. This is a mandatory reporting duty. It is not discretionary, and it must not be delayed for an internal review.

definitions.definition: Taking, secreting, appropriating, obtaining or retaining an elder's or dependent adult's money, property or other assets by deception, undue influence or for a wrongful use. In this policy it includes pressuring a client for gifts, loans or changes to a will.
The adult clients [AGENCY NAME] serves who are protected by the mandated-reporting duty in WIC §15630.
Money, goods, services, favors or other items of value given to a staff member by a client or the client's family, other than a nominal item described in the procedures.
Cash the client provides for a specific purchase that the aide makes for the client.
A homemade food item or a handwritten card offered once and openly, which the aide reports to the supervisor.

procedures: At hire and annually, the Administrator or designee trains every aide and staff member on this policy. Each person signs an acknowledgment that is placed in the personnel record.

Before services begin, the Client Care Supervisor gives the client or representative a written notice saying that staff may not accept gifts, loans, bequests, or power of attorney. The notice also says aides do not use bank cards or PINs, and that errand money is receipted. The notice is part of the service agreement packet.

Staff must decline any gift, loan, bequest or request to be named as agent, beneficiary or joint account holder. The aide may politely say that agency policy does not permit it. Nominal items may be accepted only if the aide reports them to the supervisor on the same day. The supervisor records them in the client record.

If a client or family member insists on giving a gift, or offers to name an aide in a will or power of attorney, the aide reports it to the Client Care Supervisor the same day. The supervisor documents it and may reassign the aide if undue influence is a concern.

Aides do not borrow money or property from clients. They do not lend their own money to clients. They do not buy, sell or trade items with clients, and they do not ask clients for money for any reason.

Aides do not take, hold, copy or use a client's bank card, credit or debit card, checkbook, online banking login or PIN. If a purchase requires a card, the client pays in person or a family member or the client's representative handles payment. An aide may accompany the client to the store but does not enter the PIN or sign for the client.

When a client gives an aide cash for shopping or an errand, the aide counts the cash with the client and writes the amount on the agency Errand Money Log. The client or representative initials the entry. If the client cannot initial, the aide notes the reason and the supervisor is told.

After the purchase, the aide obtains the itemized store receipt and returns the receipt and all change to the client. The aide and the client both sign the Errand Money Log showing the starting amount, amount spent and change returned. The aide does not keep any change or retain any items.

Aides do not pay bills, write checks for the client, make deposits or withdrawals, or manage accounts. If a client needs help with correspondence or mail, the aide may read or write as the client directs. The aide does not handle the client's finances.

Aides do not take client property out of the home except purchases made for the client as directed. They do not move valuables. They do not hold keys unless the client or representative gives written authorization on the service plan. The supervisor tracks any authorized keys on a key log.

Aides report missing or damaged client property to the Client Care Supervisor the same day. The supervisor completes an incident report under SAF-02 within 24 hours. If theft or exploitation is reasonably suspected, the supervisor follows the reporting steps below.

Any staff member who observes, knows of or reasonably suspects financial abuse of a client, or whom a client tells about it, must make a report immediately or as soon as practicably possible. The report is made by telephone or confidential internet tool to the county adult protective services agency or local law enforcement. The staff member makes the report personally and may not delegate it. The staff member may also tell the supervisor, but the supervisor's approval is not required before reporting.

The reporter submits the written or internet report within 2 working days of the telephone report. The reporter gives a copy to the Administrator or designee. The Administrator or designee files it in a confidential report file, not in the personnel record of the accused.

The Administrator or designee ensures that no staff member is retaliated against for reporting. The Administrator also separates the accused aide from the client's care during the review by suspending the assignment, as set out in PER-09.
The Scheduler/Registry and Billing Coordinator checks monthly that Errand Money Logs are returned and complete. The Coordinator forwards any missing or incomplete logs to the Client Care Supervisor.
The Client Care Supervisor reviews errand receipts and money logs during supervisory visits under SVC-03 and compares them with what the client says.
At least annually, the Administrator reviews financial-exploitation incidents, near misses and reports. The Administrator adjusts training and procedures as needed through GOV-05.

responsibilities.duty: Decline gifts, loans, wills and power of attorney. Never handle bank cards or PINs. Use the Errand Money Log and receipts. Report suspected financial abuse immediately to APS or law enforcement, and follow with the written report within 2 working days.
Gives clients the gift and money notice, reviews logs and receipts, investigates property complaints, completes incident reports and arranges reassignment when needed.
Collects and checks Errand Money Logs monthly and reports gaps. Ensures no billing for tasks not performed.
Trains staff, ensures timely mandated reports, protects reporters from retaliation, and reviews trends annually.
Provides resources to enforce this policy and supports the Administrator in acting on any suspected exploitation.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy (personnel record)
Client notice on gifts, money and property, acknowledged in the service agreement packet
Errand Money Log with signatures and attached receipts
